Third: Muqatil said: He knows what was before He created them and what will be after their creation. The real meaning is that they move under His power in His dominion, and He encompasses them. If this is their state, how can they deserve worship, and how can they come forward before God, Exalted, and intercede for one whom God has not permitted Him to intercede for? Then He clarified this meaning by saying: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves,﴾ that is, for one who is acceptable to God. ﴿And they are fearful out of awe of Him﴾ that is, out of their fear of Him. The verbal noun is here construed as an object of the verb (i.e., "their fear of Him" is read as "their awe of Him"). ﴿Fearful (mushfiqun)﴾ means fearing, not feeling secure from His plan.
It is related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that: "He saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, on the night of the Ascension, prostrate like a felt mat out of fear of God, Exalted." A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted.﴾ [Al-Naba: 38]

As for His saying, Exalted: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him," We shall recompense him with Hell,﴾ the meaning is that whoever among the angels says that statement, We shall requite that speaker with this recompense. This does not indicate that they said that or that they actually said it; it is close to His saying: ﴿If you were to associate partners with God, your deeds would surely be nullified.﴾ [Al-Zumar: 65] Here there are issues:

The first issue: These attributes indicate servitude and are incompatible with being begotten, for several reasons. First: When they went to such lengths in obedience that they say no word and do no deed except by His command, these are attributes of servants, not attributes of sons. Second: Since He, glory be to Him, knows the secrets of the angels, while they do not know the secrets of God, Exalted, the god deserving worship must be He, not these angels. This proof is the very same as what Jesus, peace be upon him, stated in His saying: ﴿You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 116] Third: They do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and one who is a god or a son of God would not be such. Fourth: They are in the utmost state of fear and apprehension, and that is nothing but the attribute of servants. Fifth: By His saying: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him," We shall recompense him with Hell,﴾ God alerted that their state is the state of all other accountable servants regarding promise and threat, so how could it be valid for them to be gods?

The second issue: The Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites, a rationalist theological school) argued with His saying: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ that intercession in the Hereafter does not belong to the people of major sins, because one does not say of the people of major sins that God approves of them. The answer: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and al-Dahhak said: ﴿Except for those whom He approves﴾ means those who say, "There is no god but God." Know that this verse is among the strongest proofs for us in establishing intercession for the people of major sins. Its demonstration is that whoever says, "There is no god but God," God has approved of him in that, and when it is true that God has approved of him in that, it is true that God has approved of him, because whenever a composite is true, each of its parts is necessarily true. When it is established that God has approved of him, it is necessary that he fall under this verse. Thus it is established by the argument we have stated that this verse is among the strongest proofs for us, according to what Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, established.

The third issue: This verse indicates three matters. First: it indicates that the angels are accountable, from His saying: ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command,﴾ ﴿and they are fearful out of awe of Him,﴾ and from the threat. Second: it also indicates that the angels are infallible (ma'sumun), because He said: ﴿and they act by His command.﴾ Third: Qadi Abd al-Jabbar said: His saying ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ indicates that every wrongdoer will be recompensed by God with Hell, as He threatened the angels with it, and this necessitates a definite judgment that He, Exalted, does not forgive the people of major sins in the Hereafter. The answer: At most, this general wording suggests a threat, and it is counterbalanced by the general wordings of promise.

[Page 138]

[Page 140]

Its statement (may He be exalted): ﴿Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, then We parted them, and made from water every living thing? Will they not believe?﴾ ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains lest it shake with them, and We made in it broad pathways, that they may be guided.﴾ ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling, yet they turn away from its signs.﴾ ﴿It is He who created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each floating in an orbit.﴾

Know that He, glorified and exalted, has now begun the proofs that point to the existence of the Maker (al-Sani'). These proofs also indicate that He is free from partners, because they indicate the occurrence of the wondrous arrangement in the world, and the existence of two gods would necessitate the occurrence of corruption. Thus these proofs point, from one aspect, to the oneness of God (tawhid), so they serve as a confirmation of what came before. In them there is also a refutation of the idol-worshippers, in that a God capable of creating such noble creatures, how can it be rational for them to turn away from His worship to the worship of a stone that neither harms nor benefits? This is the connection of this verse to what precedes it. Know also that He, glorified and exalted, mentions here six types of proofs:

The first type: His saying: ﴿Have those who disbelieve not seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, then We parted them﴾. On this there are several issues:

The first issue: Ibn Kathir read ﴿ألَمْ يَرَ﴾ without the waw, while the rest read it with the waw. The inclusion of the waw indicates the conjunction of this statement with a matter that preceded it. The author of al-Kashshaf said: it is also read ratqan (رَتَقًا) with a fatha on the ta', and both mean the passive, like khulf (خُلْف) and naqd (نَقْض), that is: they were joined (مَرْتُوقَتَيْنِ). If you ask: the verbal noun ratq (الرَّتْق) is suitable to stand in place of "joined" (مَرْتُوقَتَيْنِ) because it is a verbal noun, so what is the case of ratq? I say: it is by way of an implied qualifier, that is: they were a thing, ratq (شَيْئًا رَتْقًا).

The second issue: One may ask: the meaning of "seeing" in His saying ﴿Have those who disbelieve not seen﴾ is either seeing (with the eyes) or knowing. The first is problematic: firstly, because the people did not see them in that state at all; secondly, because of His saying: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ (18:51). As for knowing, it is problematic, because bodies are capable of being parted and joined in themselves, so judging them as joined first and parted afterward has no path to knowledge except revelation, and the debate is with the disbelievers who deny prophethood, so how is it permissible to rely on this kind of argument? The answer: the meaning of seeing is knowing. As for the question raised, its answer comes in several ways. One: we establish the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) by all the other miracles, then we argue from His saying, and then we take it as a proof of the arrangement of the world and the absence of corruption in it, and this confirms the aforementioned indication of tawhid (oneness). Second: ratq and fatq may be understood as the possibility of joining and parting, and reason indicates this, because bodies are apt to be joined and separated, so the specification of their being joined rather than separated, or the reverse, requires a specifier. Third: the Jews and Christians knew this, for it came in the Torah that God created a jewel, then looked at it with the eye of awe, and it became water, then He created the heavens and the earth from it and parted them. There was a kind of friendship between the idol-worshippers and the Jews because of their shared enmity toward Muhammad (ﷺ), so God argued against them with this proof, on the basis that they accept the Jews' statement on this matter.

The third issue: He said ﴿kanatā ratqan﴾ (كانَتا رَتْقًا, "they were a joined mass") and did not say kunna ratqan (كُنَّ رَتْقًا) because "the heavens" (السَّماوات) is a plural form, but what is meant by it is the singular that denotes the genus. Al-Akhfash said: "the heavens" is a kind, and "the earth" is a kind. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ (35:41). From this is the saying of people: "We reconciled between the two groups," and "Two black sheep passed by us," because this herd is a flock of sheep and that is a flock of sheep.

The fourth issue: In language, ratq means blocking, it is said: "I joined the thing (ratagtu al-shay'), so it became joined (irtataqa)." Fatq means separating between two things that were stuck together. Al-Zajjaj said: ratq is a verbal noun, and the meaning is "they were things possessing joining (dhawatay ratq)." Al-Mufaddal said: the reason He did not say "kānatā ratqayn" (رَتْقَيْنِ) is like His saying: ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾ (21:8), because each one of them is a body in the same way, and in what we are discussing, each one of them is a ratq.

The fifth issue: The commentators differed on the meaning of ratq and fatq, in several views:

One: This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and a report from Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them): the meaning is that they were one thing, joined together, then Allah separated them, raised the heaven to where it is, and left the earth where it is. This view entails that the creation of the earth preceded the creation of the heaven, because when He separated them, He left the earth where it is and raised the heavenly parts upward. Ka'b said: Allah created the heavens and the earth joined together, then He created a wind that passed between them, and parted them with it.

Two: This is the view of Abu Salih and Mujahid: the meaning is that the heavens were elevated, and then they were made seven heavens, and likewise the earths.

Three: This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, and most of the commentators: the heavens and the earth were a joined mass in terms of being level and solid, then Allah split the sky with rain and the earth with plants and trees. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿By the sky with its returning rain﴾ ﴿And by the earth that splits open﴾ (86:11-12). They preferred this view over all the others by His saying after that: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾, and that is not fitting unless the water has a connection to what preceded, and it is not so unless what is meant is what we have mentioned. If it is said: this view is weak, because rain does not descend from the heavens but from one heaven, which is the lowest heaven, we say: the plural form was used for it because every piece of it is a heaven, as one says: "a garment of many patches" (ثَوْبٌ أخْلاقٌ) and "a cooking pot in tens" (بُرْمَةٌ أعْشارٌ). Know that according to this interpretation it is permissible to take "seeing" as literal sight.

Four: The view of Abu Muslim al-Isfahani: it is permissible that by fatq is meant bringing into existence and manifesting, like His saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ (6:14), and His saying: ﴿He said: "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who originated them"﴾ (21:56). So He reported about bringing into existence with the word fatq, and about the state before bringing into existence with the word ratq. I say: its realization is that non-existence is pure negation, so there are no distinct essences or separate entities in it, but it is like one continuous, uniform matter. When the realities come into existence, at the moment of existence and coming-to-be, some of them become distinguished from others and some separate from others. By this way it is good to make ratq a metaphor for non-existence and fatq a metaphor for existence.

Five: The night precedes the day, as in His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ (36:37). The heavens and the earth were first dark, then Allah parted them by manifesting the seeing day. If it is said: which of these sayings is most fitting to the apparent meaning? We say: the apparent meaning requires that the sky, in what it is, and the earth, in what it is, were a joined mass. It is not possible for them to be so unless both exist, and ratq is the opposite of fatq. If fatq is separation, then ratq must be adherence. By this way the fourth and fifth views become weaker, and the first view becomes the best of the views, followed by the second view, which is that each of them was a joined mass, so He parted them by making each of them seven, and followed by the third view, which is that they were solid without cracks or gaps, so He split them so that rain would descend from the sky and plants would appear on the earth.

The sixth issue: The indication of these views for the establishment of the Maker and His oneness is clear, because no one is able to do the like of that. The most likely view is that He created them joined for the benefit of the angels, then when Allah settled the earth with its people, He made them parted for the benefit of the servants.

* * *

The second type of proofs: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made from water every living thing. Will they not believe?﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying "wa-ja'alnā" (وجَعَلْنا) cannot be other than transitive to one object or to two. If it is transitive to one, the meaning is "We created from water every animal," like His saying: ﴿And Allah created every creature from water﴾ (24:45), or as if We created it from water because of its extreme need for it, its love for it, and its lack of patience without it, like His saying: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ (21:37). If it is transitive to two, the meaning is "We made every living thing by means of a cause of water that it cannot do without." From this kind is the particle min (مِن) in his, peace be upon him, saying: "I am not of frivolity, and frivolity is not of me." It was also read ḥayyan (حَيًّا), and it is then the second object.

The second issue: One may ask: how did He say "We created from water every animal," when He said: ﴿And the jinn We created before from the fire of scorching wind﴾ (15:27), and it has come in reports that Allah created the angels from light, and He said regarding Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿And when you shape from clay what is like the form of a bird by My permission, then you breathe into it and it becomes a bird by My permission﴾ (5:110), and He said regarding Adam: ﴿He created him from dust﴾ (3:59)? The answer: although the wording is general, the restricting indicator is present, for the proof must be observed and perceptible in order to be closer to the intended purpose. By this way the angels, the jinn, Adam, and the story of Jesus, peace be upon them, are excluded from it, because the disbelievers did not see any of that.

The third issue: The commentators differed. Some of them said: what is meant by His saying ﴿every living thing﴾ is only animals. Others said: rather, plants and trees are included in it, because from water they became growing, and in them there is moisture, greenness, blossoms, and fruit. This view is more fitting to the intended meaning, as if He, exalted is He, said: "We parted the sky for sending down rain, and We made from it every thing on the earth, of plants and other things, living." The argument of the first view is that plants are not called living. We say: we do not concede that, and the evidence for it is His saying: ﴿How He gives life to the earth after its death﴾ (30:50). As for His saying: ﴿Will they not believe?﴾ (21:30), the meaning is: will they not believe by contemplating these proofs, so that they know by them the Creator who is not like anything else, and abandon the way of shirk (associating partners with God).

[Page 141]

Category 3: The Word of Allah, the Exalted: "And We placed in the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them" (?). Let me translate carefully.

**The third type: the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them﴾. On this there are several issues:**

**The first issue:** "lest it should shake with them" means either "for fear that it would shake with them" or "so that it would not shake with them." The particle *lā* ("not") and the first *lām* have been omitted. The omission of *lā* is permissible because there is no ambiguity, as you see in His words: ﴿so that the People of the Scripture may know﴾ [al-Hadid: 29].

**The second issue:** *al-rawāsī* (the firm mountains) are the mountains, and *al-rāsī* is that which is embedded in the earth.

**The third issue:** Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: The earth was spread out over the water, so it would tilt with its inhabitants just as a ship tilts, because it was spread over water. So Allah, the Exalted, anchored it with the heavy mountains.

* * *

**The fourth type: the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We made in it broad roads as pathways, that they might be guided﴾. On this there are several issues:**

**The first issue:** The author of *al-Kashshaf* (al-Zamakhshari) said: *al-fajj* is the wide road. If you ask: *fijāj* carries the meaning of a description, so why was it placed before *subul* and not after it, as in His words: ﴿that you may take therein roads, broad paths﴾ [Nuh: 20]? I say: It was not placed first because it is a description; rather it was made a circumstantial qualifier (*ḥāl*), like the poet's words:

*For ʿAzza, a deserted encampment, long-abandoned.*

The difference in meaning is that His words *subulan fijājan* (roads, broad paths) inform that He, glory be to Him, placed in it wide roads. As for His words *fijājan subulan*, they inform that He, glory be to Him, when He created it, made it in that state. Thus this verse is an explanation of what was left ambiguous in the first verse.

**The second issue:** Regarding His words ﴿in it﴾ there are two views. One: it refers to the mountains, meaning "and We made in the mountains, which are the firm mountains, broad roads as pathways." This is the view of Muqatil, al-Dahhak, and a report from ʿAtaʾ from Ibn ʿAbbas, and from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The mountains were joined together, and when Allah drowned the people of Nuh, He split them into broad roads and made in them pathways. Two: it refers to the earth, meaning "and We made in the earth broad roads, which are the routes and paths." This is the view of al-Kalbi.

**The third issue:** His words ﴿that they may be guided﴾ mean "in order that they may be guided," since doubt is not permissible for Allah, the Exalted.

**The fourth issue:** Regarding *yahtadūna* (they may be guided) there are two views. The first: that they may be guided to the lands. The second: that they may be guided to the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, through reasoning. The Mu'tazila said: This interpretation indicates that He, the Exalted, intended guidance from all the responsible beings. The discussion of this has already passed. There is a third view: that guidance to the lands and guidance to the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, share a single common concept, which is the basic meaning of guidance, so the word is understood in that shared sense. In that case the verse encompasses both matters, and it does not follow that a shared term is used in both of its meanings at once.

**The fifth type: His saying, ﴿And We made the heaven a protected roof, yet they turn away from its signs﴾. On this verse there are several issues:**

**First issue:** He called the heaven a "roof" (saqf) because it is to the earth what a roof is to a house.

[Page 143]

**Second issue:** Regarding "protected" (mahfuz), there are two opinions. The first is that it is protected from falling and collapsing, which are the kinds of things that happen to other roofs, as in His saying: ﴿And He holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth, except by His permission﴾ [al-Hajj: 65]; and He said: ﴿And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command﴾ [al-Rum: 25]; and God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease﴾ [Fatir: 41]; and He said: ﴿And their preservation does not burden Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. The second is that it is protected from the devils (shayatin), as God Most High said: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17]. Then, on this second point, there are two opinions. The first is that it is protected from the devils by the angels. The second is that it is protected from the devils by the stars. The first opinion is stronger, because reading the signs in this way adds greatness to this blessing, since He, glory be to Him, is as if He undertook its protection and its not falling upon those who are responsible (mukallafin). This is unlike the second opinion, because the heaven would not be in need of protection from the eavesdropping of the jinn.

**Third issue:** God Most High's saying ﴿yet they turn away from its signs﴾ means: from what God Most High has placed in it of proofs and lessons, in its movements, the manner and directions of its movements, its risings and settings, the connections of some of its parts with others and their separations, according to a upright reckoning and a wondrous arrangement, which indicate perfect wisdom and overwhelming power.

**Fourth issue:** It was read as "ʿan ayatiha" (in the singular, "its sign"), and the intended meaning is the category (jins). That is, they are attentive to what reaches them from the heaven of worldly benefits, such as being illuminated by its moon and guided by its stars, and the life of the earth by its rains; yet they turn away from its being a clear sign of the existence of the Creator and His oneness.

* * *

**The sixth type: His saying, ﴿And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit swimming﴾.** On this verse there are several issues:

**First issue:** Know that when He, glory be to Him, said ﴿yet they turn away from its signs﴾, He detailed those signs here. This is because, if God Most High had created the heaven and the earth but had not created the sun and the moon, by which night and day would appear, and by which benefits would appear through the alternation of heat and cold, the blessings of God Most High upon His servants would not have been complete. Rather, that completeness comes through their movements in their orbits (aflak). Therefore He said: ﴿each in an orbit swimming﴾. The explanation is that we say: it has been established by observation (arsad) that the stars have various movements. Among them is a movement that encompasses them all, proceeding from the east to the west, which is the daily movement of the sun. Then the majority of the philosophers and the astronomers (ashab al-hay'a) said: here is another movement, from the west to the east. They said it is apparent in the seven wandering planets (sayyarah) and hidden in the fixed stars (thabitah). They proved this by our finding that the wandering planets, whenever one of them that is faster in movement is in conjunction with one that is slower, afterwards it advances ahead of it toward the east. This is quite evident in the moon, for it appears a day or two after conjunction on the western side, at a distance from the sun, and then each night it grows further from it until it stands opposite it at about the middle of the month. And every star that is to the east of it on its path along the zodiac (buruj) draws closer to it each night. Then when it reaches it, it covers it with its eastern edge, and those stars are eclipsed from it by its western edge. So we know that these wandering stars have a movement from the west to the east. Likewise we found that the fixed stars have a slow movement along the succession of the zodiacal signs, so we know that they have a movement from the west to the east. This is what they said, and we disagreed with them on it, and we said: that is impossible. For if the sun, for example, were moving by its own essence from the west to the east with a slow movement, and there is no doubt that it is moving by means of the daily movement from the west to the east, it would follow that a single body is moving with two movements in two different directions at once, and that is impossible, because movement toward a direction requires the moving object's arrival in the direction it moves toward. So if a single body moved at once in two directions, it would follow that it is present at once in two places, and that is impossible.

[Page 144]

If it is said: why would it not be permissible to say that the sun, while moving toward the eastern side, ceases its movement toward the western side, and vice versa? Also, what you have mentioned is refuted by the movement of a millstone in one direction while the ant upon it moves in the opposite direction. We reply: as for the first, it does not hold according to your principles, because the movements of the orbits are, in your view, protected from cessation. As for the second, it is a possible example, whereas what we have mentioned is a conclusive proof, so they do not conflict. As for what they argued to show that the stars have a movement from the west to the east, it is weak. For it may be said: why would it not be permissible to say that all the stars are moving from the east to the west, but some of them are slower than others, so that some of them fall behind others because of that lag, and thus it is supposed that they are moving in the opposite direction? For example, the great orbit (al-falak al-a'zam) completes one full rotation from the first day to the beginning of the second day, and the orbit of the fixed stars completes a full rotation from the first day to the beginning of the second day, except for an amount of one second. So it is supposed that the orbit of the fixed stars moved in the other direction by one second, but that is not so; rather, it lagged behind by one second. On this assumption, all directions are eastward, and the fastest of them is the daily movement; next in speed is the orbit of the fixed stars, then Saturn, and so on until we reach the orbit of the moon, which is the slowest of the orbits in movement. What we have said, together with what the mentioned proof supports, is closer to the order of existence. For on this assumption the limit of movement is the encompassing orbit, which is the great orbit, and the limit of stillness is the body that is at the greatest distance, which is the earth. Moreover, whatever is closer to the encompassing orbit is faster in movement, and whatever is farther from it is slower. This is what we say concerning the movements of the orbits in their longitudes. As for their movements in their latitudes, these are evident, and they result from the differences in their inclinations toward the north and the south. Having established this, we say: if the stars had no movement in inclination, the influence would be restricted to a single region, so the other regions would be empty of the benefits that come from it, and whatever is near it would have similar conditions, and the force there would be of a single quality. If it were hot, it would destroy the moistures, transforming them all into fire. In sum, the place that lies opposite the path of the stars would have one quality, the line that does not face it would have another quality, and the line between them would have yet another quality. So in one place there would be perpetual winter, in which there is air and dust; in another place perpetual summer, which causes burning; and in another place spring or autumn in which ripening would not be completed. And even if there were no successive returns, and the star moved slowly, the inclination would be of little benefit and its influence would be excessively intense, and it would be close to the condition of there being no inclination at all. And if the stars were faster in movement than these, the benefits would not be complete and would not be perfected. But when there is an inclination that holds the movement in one direction for a period and then shifts to another direction to the extent needed, and remains in each direction for a while, its influence is thereby completed, such that it remains preserved from the two extremes of excess and deficiency. In sum, the intellects stand only at a little of the secrets of created things. So glory be to the Creator who governs with perfect wisdom and with a power that is not limited.

**Second issue:** It is not permissible to say ﴿and each in an orbit swimming﴾ without the stars entering the statement along with the sun and the moon, in order to establish the meaning of plurality and the meaning of totality. So the stars, even though they were not mentioned first, become mentioned by the return of this pronoun to them. And God knows best.

**Third issue:** In the language of the Arabs, falak (orbit) is anything that revolves, and its plural is aflak. The intellectuals (ʿuqala) differed about it. Some said: the falak is not a body, but is rather the path (madar) of these stars, and this is the view of al-Dahhak. Most said: rather, they are bodies upon which the stars revolve, and this is closer to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. Then they differed about its nature. Some said: the falak is a restrained wave in which the sun, the moon, and the stars flow. Al-Kalbi said: it is gathered water in which the stars flow, and he argued that swimming occurs only in water. We reply: we do not concede that, for it is said of a horse that stretches its forelegs while running that it "swims." The majority of the philosophers and the astronomers (ashab al-hay'a) said: they are solid bodies, neither heavy nor light, not receptive to splitting, joining, growth, or decay. As for discussion of the philosophers, it is mentioned in books suited to it. The truth is that there is no way to know the attributes of the heavens except through revelation (khabar).

[Page 145]

**Fourth issue:** People differed about the movements of the stars, and the possible views on this are three. **The sixth type: His saying, ﴿And it is He who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each in an orbit swimming﴾.** On this verse there are several issues:

**First issue:** Know that when He, glory be to Him, said ﴿yet they turn away from its signs﴾, He detailed those signs here. This is because, if God Most High had created the heaven and the earth but had not created the sun and the moon, by which night and day would appear, and by which benefits would appear through the alternation of heat and cold, the blessings of God Most High upon His servants would not have been complete. Rather, that completeness comes through their movements in their orbits (aflak). Therefore He said: ﴿each in an orbit swimming﴾. The explanation is that we say: it has been established by observation (arsad) that the stars have various movements. Among them is a movement that encompasses them all, proceeding from the east to the west, which is the daily movement of the sun. Then the majority of the philosophers and the astronomers (ashab al-hay'a) said: here is another movement, from the west to the east. They said it is apparent in the seven wandering planets (sayyarah) and hidden in the fixed stars (thabitah). They proved this by our finding that the wandering planets, whenever one of them that is faster in movement is in conjunction with one that is slower, afterwards it advances ahead of it toward the east. This is quite evident in the moon, for it appears a day or two after conjunction on the western side, at a distance from the sun, and then each night it grows further from it until it stands opposite it at about the middle of the month. And every star that is to the east of it on its path along the zodiac (buruj) draws closer to it each night. Then when it reaches it, it covers it with its eastern edge, and those stars are eclipsed from it by its western edge. So we know that these wandering stars have a movement from the west to the east. Likewise we found that the fixed stars have a slow movement along the succession of the zodiacal signs, so we know that they have a movement from the west to the east. This is what they said, and we disagreed with them on it, and we said: that is impossible. For if the sun, for example, were moving by its own essence from the west to the east with a slow movement, and there is no doubt that it is moving by means of the daily movement from the west to the east, it would follow that a single body is moving with two movements in two different directions at once, and that is impossible, because movement toward a direction requires the moving object's arrival in the direction it moves toward. So if a single body moved at once in two directions, it would follow that it is present at once in two places, and that is impossible.

[Page 144]

If it is said: why would it not be permissible to say that the sun, while moving toward the eastern side, ceases its movement toward the western side, and vice versa? Also, what you have mentioned is refuted by the movement of a millstone in one direction while the ant upon it moves in the opposite direction. We reply: as for the first, it does not hold according to your principles, because the movements of the orbits are, in your view, protected from cessation. As for the second, it is a possible example, whereas what we have mentioned is a conclusive proof, so they do not conflict. As for what they argued to show that the stars have a movement from the west to the east, it is weak. For it may be said: why would it not be permissible to say that all the stars are moving from the east to the west, but some of them are slower than others, so that some of them fall behind others because of that lag, and thus it is supposed that they are moving in the opposite direction? For example, the great orbit (al-falak al-a'zam) completes one full rotation from the first day to the beginning of the second day, and the orbit of the fixed stars completes a full rotation from the first day to the beginning of the second day, except for an amount of one second. So it is supposed that the orbit of the fixed stars moved in the other direction by one second, but that is not so; rather, it lagged behind by one second. On this assumption, all directions are eastward, and the fastest of them is the daily movement; next in speed is the orbit of the fixed stars, then Saturn, and so on until we reach the orbit of the moon, which is the slowest of the orbits in movement. What we have said, together with what the mentioned proof supports, is closer to the order of existence. For on this assumption the limit of movement is the encompassing orbit, which is the great orbit, and the limit of stillness is the body that is at the greatest distance, which is the earth. Moreover, whatever is closer to the encompassing orbit is faster in movement, and whatever is farther from it is slower. This is what we say concerning the movements of the orbits in their longitudes. As for their movements in their latitudes, these are evident, and they result from the differences in their inclinations toward the north and the south. Having established this, we say: if the stars had no movement in inclination, the influence would be restricted to a single region, so the other regions would be empty of the benefits that come from it, and whatever is near it would have similar conditions, and the force there would be of a single quality. If it were hot, it would destroy the moistures, transforming them all into fire. In sum, the place that lies opposite the path of the stars would have one quality, the line that does not face it would have another quality, and the line between them would have yet another quality. So in one place there would be perpetual winter, in which there is air and dust; in another place perpetual summer, which causes burning; and in another place spring or autumn in which ripening would not be completed. And even if there were no successive returns, and the star moved slowly, the inclination would be of little benefit and its influence would be excessively intense, and it would be close to the condition of there being no inclination at all. And if the stars were faster in movement than these, the benefits would not be complete and would not be perfected. But when there is an inclination that holds the movement in one direction for a period and then shifts to another direction to the extent needed, and remains in each direction for a while, its influence is thereby completed, such that it remains preserved from the two extremes of excess and deficiency. In sum, the intellects stand only at a little of the secrets of created things. So glory be to the Creator who governs with perfect wisdom and with a power that is not limited.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 35–36:

Page 146
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We did not grant to any human before you immortality. So if you die, will they be immortal?﴾ ﴿Every soul shall taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as a trial; and to Us you will be returned.﴾ ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" while they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾

Know that when He, glorified and exalted, had argued from the six things that we explained in the previous section, and those things were among the foundations of worldly blessings, He followed it with what draws attention to the fact that He made this world such that it is not meant to last and endure, nor for whoever the world was created for to remain in it. Rather, He, glorified and exalted, created it for trial and testing, and so that through it one may reach the Hereafter, which is the abode of eternity.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We did not grant to any human before you immortality﴾, there are three aspects to it. The first: Muqatil said that some people were saying that Muhammad ﷺ would not die, so this verse was revealed. The second: they expected that he would die and would gloat over his death, so God, exalted is He, negated that gloating from him by this, i.e., God decreed that no human be made eternal in this world. So neither you nor they are anything but subject to death. "So if you die, will they remain?" No. And in its meaning is the saying of the poet:

So say to those who gloat over us: "Wait; the gloaters will meet what we met."

The third: it is possible that, since it became clear that he, peace be upon him, is the Seal of the Prophets, someone might suppose that he would not die, for if he died his law would change. So God, exalted is He, drew attention to the fact that his condition is like the condition of other prophets, peace be upon them, regarding death.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾, there are discussions concerning it:

The first discussion: this generality is specified, for He, exalted is He, is a soul, according to His saying: ﴿You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116], although death is not applicable to Him, and likewise inanimate objects have souls yet do not die. A specified general (al-'amm al-makhsus) is a proof, so it remains acted upon regarding what is other than these things. This refutes the claim of the philosophers that human spirits, separate intellects and celestial souls do not die. The second: tasting cannot be taken in its literal sense here, because death is not of the category of food that is tasted; rather, tasting is a special kind of perception, so it is permissible to make it a metaphor for perception in general. As for death, what is meant by it here is its preliminaries of great pains, because death before entering existence cannot be perceived, and while one is alive the person becomes dead, and the dead perceive nothing. The third: the idafah (construct) in "dha'iqatu al-mawt" is in the sense of separation (infisal), because it refers to what is future, like His saying: ﴿not violating the game﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 1], and ﴿an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95].

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verse 37–43:

[Page 148]
His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to mock.﴾

As for His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, there are several issues.

The first issue: Regarding what is meant by "man" (al-insan), there are two opinions. One is that it refers to the species (al-naw'). The other is that it refers to a specific individual. As for the first opinion, its explanation is that they were hastening the punishment of Allah, Exalted is He, and His signs that compel knowledge and acknowledgment: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise?"﴾ So He intended to restrain them from that. He first censured man for excessive haste, then forbade and restrained them, as if He said: It is not strange that you hasten, for you are inclined to that; it is your nature and disposition. If it is said: The introduction of a speech must be appropriate to the speech, and that man was created from haste suits his being excused for it, so why did He make the statement ﴿so do not ask Me to hasten﴾ follow from this introduction? We say: Because the more intense the obstacle, the more perfect the ability to oppose it. So, by this, He, glorified is He, alerted that abandoning haste is a noble and exalted state, one to be desired. As for the second opinion, that the intended meaning is a specific individual, there are two views on this. One is that the intended one is Adam, peace be upon him. This is the view of Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, Muqatil and al-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid who said: Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, after everything else, at the end of Friday's day. When the spirit entered his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "My Lord, hasten my creation before sunset." Layth said: That is His statement: ﴿Man was created of haste.﴾ And from al-Suddi: When He breathed the spirit into him and it entered his head, he sneezed, and the angels said to him: "Say: All praise is for Allah," so he said that, and Allah said to him: "May your Lord have mercy on you." When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise, and when the spirit entered his belly, he desired food, so he leapt, before the spirit reached his feet, toward the fruits of Paradise. This is what passed on haste to his offspring. The second view: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said in the narration of 'Ata': This verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and "man" refers to him. Know that the first opinion is more preferable, because the purpose is to censure the people, and that is only achieved if we take the word "man" to refer to the species.

The second issue: Among the exegetes, some have taken this verse according to its apparent meaning, and some have reversed it. As for the first group, they have several statements. One of them is the statement of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun): that His statement ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ means he was created hasty, and this is by way of exaggeration, just as one says of an intelligent man: "He is a fire that blazes." The Arabs sometimes name a person by what is abundant in him, so they say: "You are nothing but eating and sleeping," and "He is nothing but coming and going." The poet said:

Whenever she is mentioned, until she becomes heedless, she is nothing but coming and going.

This interpretation is supported by His statement: ﴿And man has ever been hasty.﴾ [al-Isra' 11]. Al-Mubarrad said: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ means that haste is part of his nature, like His statement: ﴿He created you from weakness﴾ [al-Rum 54], meaning weak. The second: Abu 'Ubayd said: "al-'ajal" is mud in the dialect of Himyar, and they recited:

And the palm tree stands between water and mud.

[Page 149]
The third: al-Akhfash said: "min 'ajal" means "from a hastening of the command," which is His statement "Be!" The fourth: "min 'ajal" means "from weakness," according to al-Hasan. As for those who reversed it, they said the meaning is: haste was created from man, like His statement: ﴿And on the Day the disbelievers are exposed to the Fire﴾, meaning the Fire is exposed to them. The first opinion is closer to the correct one, and this reversal is the most remote of the opinions, because if the speech can be understood in a sound meaning while still in its order, it is more fitting to take it in that sense rather than to say it is reversed. Also, the statement "haste was created from man" contains several forms of metaphor, so what is the benefit in changing the arrangement to something that goes in the same metaphorical direction?

The third issue: Someone might say: They sought the promise in the manner of denial, and one whose state is this is not truly hasty. We say: Their haste in this manner is more deserving of censure, because if a person is censured for hastening a matter that is known, then being censured for hastening what is not known to him is more fitting. Also, their hastening for what He threatened them with, the punishment of the Hereafter or the destruction of this world, implies hastening death, and they knew this, so they were hasty in reality.

* * *

As for His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten﴾, they differed about what is meant by "signs," with several opinions. One: They are the sudden destruction in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter; for this reason He said: ﴿so do not ask Me to hasten﴾, meaning they will come without doubt at their appointed time. Two: They are the proofs of monotheism and the truthfulness of the Messenger. Three: They are the traces of the past generations in al-Sham and Yemen. The first is closer to the context.

As for His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾, know that this is the blameworthy haste, mentioned in the manner of mockery, and it is like His statement: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 53]. So Exalted is He made clear that they say this out of their ignorance and heedlessness. Then, glorified is He, mentioned two aspects to remove this grief from the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The first: by clarifying the severe punishment due to the one who engages in this mockery, He said: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: The response to "law" (if only) is omitted, and "hina" is the object of "ya'lam" (know), meaning: If only they knew the time about which they ask with their statement "When is this promise?" It is a time of hardship and severity, in which the Fire encompasses them from in front and from behind, so they are unable to ward it off from themselves, and they will not find a helper to help them, by His statement: ﴿Who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?﴾ [Ghafir 29], because of their state of disbelief, mockery and hastening. But their ignorance of it is what made it easy for them. The omission of the response was good because what preceded it indicates it. This is more eloquent, and similar to it are: ﴿And if only those who did wrong could see﴾ [al-Baqarah 165], ﴿And if you could see when those who disbelieved are taken in death﴾ [al-Anfal 50], ﴿And if there had been a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved﴾ [al-Ra'd 31]. He specified the faces and backs because the touch of punishment is most severe upon them, and because these two are most often mentioned in warding off harm from the self. Then, when He, exalted is He, explained the severity of this punishment, He clarified that the time of its coming is unknown to them; rather, the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they are not expecting it nor prepared for its matter, so it will bewilder them, meaning it will leave them confused and standing still, unable to find a way to repel it, nor a means to turn away from what comes to them from it, and they will not be given respite, meaning they will not be granted time for repentance or excuse.

Know that Allah, Exalted is He, did not inform the accountable ones of the time of death and the Resurrection because of the wisdom in that; for a person, when this is concealed, is more cautious and closer to making amends. Then, glorified is He, mentioned the second aspect for removing grief from the heart of His Messenger, and said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to mock.﴾

[Page 150]
The meaning: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked﴾, O Muhammad, just as your people mocked you, ﴿but﴾ it descended upon and encompassed ﴿those who mocked them, that which they used to mock﴾, meaning the punishment for their mockery. "Haqa" and "haqqa" have the same meaning, like "zalla" and "zalla" (both meaning to slip). In this there is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ. The meaning is: thus, the consequence of their mockery will similarly descend upon these people.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verse 37–43:

[Page 148]
His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.﴾ ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to mock.﴾

As for His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, there are several issues.

The first issue: Regarding what is meant by "man" (al-insan), there are two opinions. One is that it refers to the species (al-naw'). The other is that it refers to a specific individual. As for the first opinion, its explanation is that they were hastening the punishment of Allah, Exalted is He, and His signs that compel knowledge and acknowledgment: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise?"﴾ So He intended to restrain them from that. He first censured man for excessive haste, then forbade and restrained them, as if He said: It is not strange that you hasten, for you are inclined to that; it is your nature and disposition. If it is said: The introduction of a speech must be appropriate to the speech, and that man was created from haste suits his being excused for it, so why did He make the statement ﴿so do not ask Me to hasten﴾ follow from this introduction? We say: Because the more intense the obstacle, the more perfect the ability to oppose it. So, by this, He, glorified is He, alerted that abandoning haste is a noble and exalted state, one to be desired. As for the second opinion, that the intended meaning is a specific individual, there are two views on this. One is that the intended one is Adam, peace be upon him. This is the view of Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi, Muqatil and al-Dahhak. Ibn Jarir and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym related from Mujahid who said: Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, after everything else, at the end of Friday's day. When the spirit entered his head but had not reached his lower body, he said: "My Lord, hasten my creation before sunset." Layth said: That is His statement: ﴿Man was created of haste.﴾ And from al-Suddi: When He breathed the spirit into him and it entered his head, he sneezed, and the angels said to him: "Say: All praise is for Allah," so he said that, and Allah said to him: "May your Lord have mercy on you." When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise, and when the spirit entered his belly, he desired food, so he leapt, before the spirit reached his feet, toward the fruits of Paradise. This is what passed on haste to his offspring. The second view: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said in the narration of 'Ata': This verse was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and "man" refers to him. Know that the first opinion is more preferable, because the purpose is to censure the people, and that is only achieved if we take the word "man" to refer to the species.

The second issue: Among the exegetes, some have taken this verse according to its apparent meaning, and some have reversed it. As for the first group, they have several statements. One of them is the statement of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun): that His statement ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ means he was created hasty, and this is by way of exaggeration, just as one says of an intelligent man: "He is a fire that blazes." The Arabs sometimes name a person by what is abundant in him, so they say: "You are nothing but eating and sleeping," and "He is nothing but coming and going." The poet said:

Whenever she is mentioned, until she becomes heedless, she is nothing but coming and going.

This interpretation is supported by His statement: ﴿And man has ever been hasty.﴾ [al-Isra' 11]. Al-Mubarrad said: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ means that haste is part of his nature, like His statement: ﴿He created you from weakness﴾ [al-Rum 54], meaning weak. The second: Abu 'Ubayd said: "al-'ajal" is mud in the dialect of Himyar, and they recited:

And the palm tree stands between water and mud.

[Page 149]
The third: al-Akhfash said: "min 'ajal" means "from a hastening of the command," which is His statement "Be!" The fourth: "min 'ajal" means "from weakness," according to al-Hasan. As for those who reversed it, they said the meaning is: haste was created from man, like His statement: ﴿And on the Day the disbelievers are exposed to the Fire﴾, meaning the Fire is exposed to them. The first opinion is closer to the correct one, and this reversal is the most remote of the opinions, because if the speech can be understood in a sound meaning while still in its order, it is more fitting to take it in that sense rather than to say it is reversed. Also, the statement "haste was created from man" contains several forms of metaphor, so what is the benefit in changing the arrangement to something that goes in the same metaphorical direction?

The third issue: Someone might say: They sought the promise in the manner of denial, and one whose state is this is not truly hasty. We say: Their haste in this manner is more deserving of censure, because if a person is censured for hastening a matter that is known, then being censured for hastening what is not known to him is more fitting. Also, their hastening for what He threatened them with, the punishment of the Hereafter or the destruction of this world, implies hastening death, and they knew this, so they were hasty in reality.

* * *

As for His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten﴾, they differed about what is meant by "signs," with several opinions. One: They are the sudden destruction in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter; for this reason He said: ﴿so do not ask Me to hasten﴾, meaning they will come without doubt at their appointed time. Two: They are the proofs of monotheism and the truthfulness of the Messenger. Three: They are the traces of the past generations in al-Sham and Yemen. The first is closer to the context.

As for His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾, know that this is the blameworthy haste, mentioned in the manner of mockery, and it is like His statement: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 53]. So Exalted is He made clear that they say this out of their ignorance and heedlessness. Then, glorified is He, mentioned two aspects to remove this grief from the heart of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The first: by clarifying the severe punishment due to the one who engages in this mockery, He said: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: The response to "law" (if only) is omitted, and "hina" is the object of "ya'lam" (know), meaning: If only they knew the time about which they ask with their statement "When is this promise?" It is a time of hardship and severity, in which the Fire encompasses them from in front and from behind, so they are unable to ward it off from themselves, and they will not find a helper to help them, by His statement: ﴿Who will help us against the might of Allah if it comes upon us?﴾ [Ghafir 29], because of their state of disbelief, mockery and hastening. But their ignorance of it is what made it easy for them. The omission of the response was good because what preceded it indicates it. This is more eloquent, and similar to it are: ﴿And if only those who did wrong could see﴾ [al-Baqarah 165], ﴿And if you could see when those who disbelieved are taken in death﴾ [al-Anfal 50], ﴿And if there had been a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved﴾ [al-Ra'd 31]. He specified the faces and backs because the touch of punishment is most severe upon them, and because these two are most often mentioned in warding off harm from the self. Then, when He, exalted is He, explained the severity of this punishment, He clarified that the time of its coming is unknown to them; rather, the Hour will come upon them suddenly while they are not expecting it nor prepared for its matter, so it will bewilder them, meaning it will leave them confused and standing still, unable to find a way to repel it, nor a means to turn away from what comes to them from it, and they will not be given respite, meaning they will not be granted time for repentance or excuse.

Know that Allah, Exalted is He, did not inform the accountable ones of the time of death and the Resurrection because of the wisdom in that; for a person, when this is concealed, is more cautious and closer to making amends. Then, glorified is He, mentioned the second aspect for removing grief from the heart of His Messenger, and said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who mocked them were enveloped by that which they used to mock.﴾

[Page 150]
The meaning: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked﴾, O Muhammad, just as your people mocked you, ﴿but﴾ it descended upon and encompassed ﴿those who mocked them, that which they used to mock﴾, meaning the punishment for their mockery. Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that the disbelievers in the Hereafter will not be able to shield their faces from the Fire with anything He had described for them, He followed this by saying that in this world too, were it not for God, exalted is He, guarding and protecting them, they would not have remained safe. So He said to His Messenger: Say to these disbelievers who mock and are deceived by what they have: ﴿Who protects you by night and by day?﴾ This is like a man saying to someone who is in his grip and has no way of escape: "Where will you flee from me? Is there any escape for you from me?" *Al-kali'* means the one who guards.

* * *

As for His words ﴿from the All-Merciful﴾, there are several issues:

The first issue: its meaning has several aspects. One is: ﴿Who protects you from the All-Merciful?﴾, that is, from what He is able to send down upon you of punishment that you deserve. The second is: from the might of God in the Hereafter. The third is: from killing, captivity and all else that God has permitted because of their disbelief. So He, glorified is He, made clear that there is no guardian for them and no one to repel these matters should He send them down upon them. Were it not for His bounty in guarding them, they would not have lived, nor would they have been granted enjoyment of this world.

The second issue: He specifically mentioned the name *al-Rahman* here as a way of guiding the answer, so that the intelligent person would say: "You are the Guardian, O our God, of all creation by Your mercy," just as in His words ﴿What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ [al-Infitar: 6]. He specifically mentioned the name *al-Karim* as a way of guiding the answer.

The third issue: He mentioned the night and the day because each of the two times has its own dangers that are specific to it. The meaning is: who guards you at night when you sleep and by day when you go about your livelihoods.

As for His words ﴿Nay, but they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord﴾, the meaning is: despite His bestowing upon them, by night and by day, protection and safeguarding, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord, which is the rational and transmitted proofs and the subtle meanings of the Qur'an. They do not reflect on any of them, so that they might know that there is no guardian for them other than Him, and they abandon the worship of idols, which have no share in guarding them or in bestowing favour upon them.

[Page 151]

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿Or have they gods who can defend them against Us? They cannot even help themselves, nor can they be accompanied by Us.﴾ Know that the *mim* here is a *silah* (a connecting particle), meaning: "Do they have gods that protect them apart from Us?" The construction is: "Do they have gods apart from Us that defend them?" and the sentence is complete. Then He described their gods as weak, saying ﴿They cannot even help themselves﴾, and this is the *khabar* (predicate) of an omitted *mubtada'* (subject), that is: these gods are unable to protect themselves from calamities. Protecting oneself takes precedence over protecting others, so if they cannot protect themselves, how could they protect others? As for His words ﴿nor can they be accompanied by Us﴾, there are two opinions. The first: al-Mazini said: "I accompanied the man" means "I prevented him," so His words ﴿nor can they be accompanied by Us﴾ derive from this, not from *suhbah* (companionship). The second: the *suhbah* here means support and assistance, and all of these are the same in meaning; one says: "God accompany you" and "God support you," and it is said to the traveller: "in the company of God" and "in the protection of God." So the meaning is: nor do they have support or assistance from Us. The conclusion is that one who is not capable of repelling calamities and is not accompanied by God with assistance, how can he be capable of anything? Then He, glorified is He, made clear His bounty upon them despite all of this, by saying: ﴿Nay, We have given enjoyment to these and their fathers until a long time passed over them﴾, meaning: what led them to turn away was only being deceived by the long respite, that is, their lives lengthened in heedlessness, so they forgot Our covenant, did not recognise the place of Our blessings, and were deceived by that.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ the meaning is: do these polytheists who are hasty for punishment not see the signs of Our power in coming to the land from its sides, seizing one after another, conquering the towns and villages around Mecca, adding them to the dominion of Muhammad (ﷺ), causing the chieftains of the polytheists who enjoy this world to die, and diminishing polytheism by destroying its people? Was there not in that a lesson for them, so that they would believe in the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and know that they cannot prevent what God wills concerning them, nor can they overcome Him? Then He said: ﴿Are they then the victors?﴾, that is: are these the victors, or are We? This is an interrogative with the meaning of affirmation and rebuke, and the meaning is: nay, We are the victors and they are the vanquished. The discussion of this verse has already passed in Surat al-Ra'd.

There are several interpretations of "reducing": First, Ibn 'Abbas, Muqatil and al-Kalbi, may God be pleased with them, said: "reducing it" means by conquering the lands. Second, Ibn 'Abbas said in another narration: he means the diminishing of its people and its blessings. Third, 'Ikrimah said: the ruin of the towns at the death of their people. Fourth: by the death of scholars. If this narration is authentic from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it should not be departed from; otherwise, the most apparent of the views is what relates to victory, which is why He said ﴿Are they then the victors?﴾. What fits this is that He diminishes it from them and adds it to the lands of Islam. Al-Qaffal said: this verse was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Mecca, so how would the scholars and jurists enter into it? God, exalted is He, made clear that all of this is among the lessons which, if they had used their intellects to consider them, would have turned away from their ignorance.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 45–47:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.﴾ ﴿And if a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them, they will surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed we have been wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners.﴾

Page 152.

Know that when He, glorified is He, repeated the proofs in the Qur'an and emphasised drawing attention to them, as mentioned earlier, He followed this with His saying: ﴿Say, "I only warn you by revelation"﴾, meaning by the Qur'an, which is the speech of your Lord. So do not suppose that this comes from me; rather, God Himself brings it to you and commanded me to warn you. When I have done what my Lord obligated upon me, and acceptance and response do not come from you, then the consequence returns upon you. He compared them, in that they did not benefit from what they heard of his warning despite its abundance and repetition, to the deaf who do not hear at all, since the purpose of warning is not merely hearing but holding fast to it by proceeding to a obligatory duty, abstaining from what is forbidden, and knowing the truth. When this purpose is not achieved, it is as if it had not been heard.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: It has been read as ﴿And the deaf do not hear the call﴾ with a ta' and with a ya', meaning: you do not make them hear, or the Messenger of God does not make them hear, or he does not make the deaf hear, whoever makes them hear. If you say: the deaf do not hear the call of a human being just as they do not hear the call of the warner, so how does He say ﴿when they are warned﴾? I say: the lam in "the deaf" is a reference to these warned people; it is for specific reference, not for the class, and the original would be "and they do not hear the call when they are warned." So the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun to indicate their deafness and their stopping their ears when they are warned, meaning they are in this state of boldness and audacity in being deaf to the signs of warning.

Then He, exalted is He, made clear that their condition will change until they come to the point that when they witness a little of what they were warned about, then at that moment they will hear, make excuses, and confess when confession no longer benefits them. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And if a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them, they will surely say, "Woe to us! Indeed we have been wrongdoers."﴾ The origin of nafh is from a gentle wind, and the meaning is: if even a small amount of God's punishment touches them, like the scent of a thing without its body, they would surely cry out "Woe!" and confess against themselves to wrongdoing.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: In "touch" (mass) and "breath" (nafha) there are three intensifications: the word "touch," the meaning of smallness and slightness in "breath" (it is said: "the animal breathed at him," meaning a light thrust of a spear; and "he breathed him with a gift," meaning he gave him a little), and the word "once."

Then God, glorified and exalted, made clear that everything that befalls them in the Hereafter will only be just; so although they wronged themselves in this world, they will not be wronged in the Hereafter. This is the meaning of His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice﴾. God described them thus because a scale may be upright or may be otherwise; so He made clear that those scales operate according to the measure of justice and equity. He confirmed this with His saying: ﴿so no soul will be wronged in anything﴾. And here are some issues:

First issue: The meaning of setting them up is bringing them forth. Al-Farra' said: "al-qist" is an attribute of the scales, although it is singular, as in your saying to a group, "you are justice." Al-Zajjaj said: "and We will set up the scales possessing equity." His saying ﴿for the Day of Resurrection﴾: al-Farra' said: "on the Day of Resurrection," and it was said: "for the people of the Day of Resurrection."

Second issue: Concerning the setting up of the scales there are two views. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "I only warn you by revelation." But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.﴾ ﴿And if a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them, they will surely say, "Woe to us! Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 48–50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (al-Furqan), and a light and a reminder for the God-conscious,﴾ ﴿those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and who are apprehensive of the Hour.﴾ ﴿And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down. Will you then deny it?﴾

Know that when He, glorified is He, spoke about the proofs of divine unity, prophethood and the Return, He began on the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, to console the Messenger, peace be upon him, for what he suffered from his people, to strengthen his heart to convey the message, and to be patient with every obstacle that stood in its way. He mentioned here several of these stories.

(The first story: the story of Moses, peace be upon him)

The connection (wajh al-ittisal) is that when He, exalted is He, commanded His Messenger ﷺ to say: ﴿I only warn you by revelation,﴾ He followed it with the statement that this is God's practice concerning the prophets before him, so He said: ﴿And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the God-conscious.﴾ They differed about the meaning of al-Furqan, in several opinions. One of them: it is the Tawrah (Torah). It was a criterion because by it one distinguishes truth from falsehood; it was a light because, by its great clarity, one reaches the paths of guidance and the ways of salvation in knowing God and knowing the laws; and it was a reminder, that is, an admonition, or a reminder of what they need in their religion and their interests, or of honour. As for the waw in His saying ﴿and a light﴾, Ikrimah related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he read ḍiyā'an (a light) without the waw, and then it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to al-Furqan. As for the well-known reading, the meaning is: We gave them the Criterion, which is the Tawrah, and We gave with it a light and a reminder for the God-conscious. The meaning is that it is in itself a light and a reminder, or that We gave both of them what it contains of laws and admonitions as a light and a reminder.

The second opinion: the intended meaning of al-Furqan is not the Tawrah. Then there are several aspects. One: from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: al-Furqan is the victory that was given to Moses, peace be upon him, like His saying: ﴿And We did not send down upon Our servant on the day of al-Furqan﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], meaning the Day of Badr, when He distinguished between truth and the other false religions. Two: it is the proof by which He separated the religion of truth from false religions, from Ibn Zayd. Three: the splitting of the sea, from al-Dahhak. Four: escaping from doubts. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Know that He, exalted is He, specified the reminder for the God-conscious only because of what is in His saying: ﴿a guidance for the God-conscious﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2].

As for His exalted saying: ﴿those who fear their Lord in the unseen﴾, the author of al-Kashshaf said: the position of alladhina (those who) is in the genitive as a descriptive qualifier, or in the accusative by way of praise, or in the nominative by way of that. As for the meaning of "the unseen" (al-ghayb), there are several aspects.
