Issue five: This indicates that the first to make the coat of mail was Dawud, and then people learned it from him. People inherited it from him, and the blessing thereby encompassed every fighter among creation until the end of time. Therefore they are obliged to thank Allah, the Exalted, for the blessing. So He said: ﴿Then, are you grateful?﴾, that is: Give thanks to Allah for what He has made easy for you of this craft. Know that when He, glorified is He, mentioned the blessings with which He favoured Dawud, He then mentioned the blessings with which He favoured Sulayman, peace be upon him. Qatadah said: Allah, the Exalted, made Sulayman inherit from Dawud his kingdom and his prophethood, and added to him two things: He subjected the wind and the devils to him.

The first blessing: His words, the Exalted: ﴿And to Sulayman [We subjected] the wind, violent, running by his command﴾. That is: We made it obedient and submissive to him, in the sense that if he willed it to be violent, it would be violent, and if he willed it to be gentle, it would be gentle, and Allah, the Exalted, subjected it in both states. If it is said: "al-'asif" means the one of severe blowing, yet Allah, the Exalted, described it as gentle in His words: ﴿Gentle, wherever he directed it﴾ [Sad 38:36]. How then can the two be combined? The answer is in two ways:

First: In itself it was gentle and pleasant, like a breeze. When it passed by his throne, it carried him far in a short time, as He said: ﴿Its morning course was a month's journey, and its evening course a month's journey﴾ [Saba' 34:12]. It combined the two: gentleness in its own nature, and violence in its action, together with its obedience to Sulayman, peace be upon him. Its blowing followed what he willed and decreed, sign after sign, and miracle after miracle.

Second: It was gentle at one time and violent at another, depending on its blowing according to his will.

Issue six: "al-Rih" and "al-Riyah" have been read in both the nominative and accusative in both forms. The nominative is on the basis of the subject (ibtida'), and the accusative is by conjunction with "al-jibal" (the mountains). If it is said: He said regarding Dawud: ﴿And We subjected the mountains along with Dawud﴾, and regarding Sulayman: ﴿And to Sulayman the wind﴾, mentioning it for Dawud with the word "ma'a" (with) and for Sulayman with the preposition "li-" (to). He also observed this order in His words: ﴿O mountains, echo with him and the birds﴾ [Saba' 34:10], and He said: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running by his command﴾ [Sad 38:36]. What is the point of singling out Dawud with the word "ma'a" and Sulayman with "li-"? We say: It is possible that because the mountain was occupied with glorification, it attained a kind of honour, so what is attributed to it is attributed with the preposition of ownership (lam al-tamlik). As for the wind, nothing proceeded from it except what functions as service, so for this reason it is attributed to Sulayman with the preposition of ownership. This is my persuasive view.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿To the land which We had blessed for the worlds﴾, that is: to proceeding to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). al-Kalbi said: It would travel from Istakhr to Syria, with Sulayman and his companions riding upon it.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 79–82 (part 2 of 2):

As for His saying, ﴿And We were Knowers of all things﴾, meaning: because of Our knowledge of things, it was valid for Us to arrange this arrangement among Our messengers, and in Our creation, and to perform these overpowering miracles.

The second favour: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him and did other work than that. And We were guardians over them﴾. There are several issues concerning it.

The first issue: the meaning is that they dived for him in the seas and extracted pearls, and went beyond that to crafts and trades, the building of cities and palaces, and the invention of wondrous industries, as He said: ﴿They made for him whatever he willed: sanctuaries, statues, and basins﴾ [Saba': 13]. As for the industries, they include the making of baths, depilatory lime, mills, glass vessels and soap.

The second issue: His saying, ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him﴾, means: "And We subjected to Solomon from among the devils those who dived for him." Thus it is in the position of the accusative (nasb, the grammatical case of the object) in coordination with "the wind". Al-Zajjaj said: "It may also be in the position of the nominative (raf', the grammatical case of the subject) in two ways:
One of them: coordination with "the wind", so that the meaning is: 'And for Solomon is the wind, and for him are those devils who dive for him.' It may also be nominative by way of inception (ibtida'), with "lahu" (for him) being the predicate (khabar)."

The third issue: it is possible that those among them who dived are the same ones who did all the other works, and it is possible that they were a separate group, all of them being included in the word "man" (those who). The first, however, is closer.

The fourth issue: the outward meaning says only that He subjected them to him. However, it has been narrated that He, exalted is He, subjected their disbelievers and not the believers, and this is closer for two reasons:
One of them: the unrestricted use of the word "devils".
The second: His saying, ﴿And We were guardians over them﴾, for a believer, when subjected to a task, does not need to be guarded lest he corrupt it; guarding is required only for the disbeliever.

The fifth issue: concerning His saying, ﴿And We were guardians over them﴾, there are several explanations:
The first: He, exalted is He, appointed over them a group of angels, or a group of believing jinn.
The second: Allah, exalted is He, subjected them by making His obedience beloved to them and making them fear disobedience to Him.
The third: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "It means that His authority remains over them, and He does to them what He wills."
If it is said: "From what were they guarded?" We say: there are three possibilities:
The first: He, exalted is He, was guarding them for him, lest they flee and leave him.
The second: al-Kalbi said: He was guarding them from stirring up anyone during his time.
The third: He was guarding them from corrupting what they had made, for their habit was to work by day and then corrupt it at night.

The sixth issue: al-Jubba'i asked himself and said: "How could these works come about for them, when their bodies are subtle and they cannot perform heavy labour, and they can only whisper?" He answered that He, glory be to Him, made their bodies dense specifically and strengthened them and increased their size, so that this would be a miracle for Solomon, peace be upon him. When Solomon died, Allah returned them to their original creation, because if He had left them in the second creation, it would have become a confusion for people, and if a pretender to prophethood had claimed prophethood and made it a proof, it would have been like the miracles of the messengers. Therefore He returned them to their original creation.
Know that this speech is invalid for several reasons:
The first: Why do you say that the jinn are bodies? Why is it not possible that there exists a created thing that is neither spatially located (mutahayyiz) nor subsisting in something spatially located, and the jinn are among such things? If you say: "If the matter were so, they would be a likeness to the Creator, exalted is He," I say: this is weak, because sharing in positive necessary attributes does not indicate sharing in what they necessitate, so how much less does sharing in negative attributes.
Granted that they are bodies, yet it is not possible for the capacity for these arduous works to be present in a subtle body. His speech is based on the premise that structure (bunyah) is a condition, and in his hand there is only weak inductive reasoning.
Granted that there must be densifying of their bodies, why do you say that there must be their return to the original creation after the death of Solomon, peace be upon him? If he says: "So that it does not lead to deception (talbis)," we say: deception does not necessarily follow, because if a pretender makes that a miracle for himself, the claimant may say: "Why is it not possible to say that the strength of their bodies was a miracle of another prophet before you?" And with the existence of this possibility, the pretender cannot use it as evidence.

Know that the bodies of this world are either dense or subtle. As for the dense, the densest bodies are stones and iron, and Allah, exalted is He, made both of them a miracle for David, peace be upon him: He made the stone speak and softened the iron. Each of them, just as it indicates monotheism and prophethood, indicates the validity of resurrection (hashr), for since He was able to bring stones to life, what is the distance in bringing bones that have decayed back to life? And since He was able to place in the finger of David, peace be upon him, the power of fire while the finger is extremely subtle, what is the distance in making dry earth into a living animal body?
The subtlest things in this world are air and fire, and Allah made both of them a miracle for Solomon, peace be upon him. As for air, it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We subjected the wind to him﴾ [Sad: 36]. As for fire, it is because the devils were created from it, and Allah, exalted is He, subjected them, so he would command them to dive into the waters, while fire is extinguished by water, yet this did not harm them. This indicates His power to bring forth the opposite from its opposite.

[Page 177]

**The Sixth Story: The Story of Ayyub (peace be upon him)**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾ ﴿So We answered him and removed what was upon him of harm, and We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾

Know that in the matter of Ayyub (peace be upon him), and in what Allah the Exalted mentions of his circumstances here and elsewhere in the Qur'an, there are lessons and proofs that are not found elsewhere. This is because Allah the Exalted, despite His great favour toward him, sent upon him a severe illness of the kind He had not sent upon anyone else, and [this was] to make it known to him, to others, and to everyone who heard of it, that this world is the field of the Hereafter, and that it is obligatory upon a person to be patient with the trials he encounters in it, to strive in discharging the right of Allah the Exalted, and to be patient in both states of adversity and ease. There are several issues concerning this:

**The first issue:** Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Ayyub (peace be upon him) was a man from the Romans. He was Ayyub ibn Anus, and he was from the descendants of Esau ibn Isaac, and his mother was from the descendants of Lot. Allah the Exalted had chosen him and made him a prophet. Along with this, He had given him a generous share of the world's bounties: livestock, gardens, and blessings, and He gave him a household and children, both sons and daughters. He was merciful to the needy, he would look after orphans and widows, and he would honour guests. He had with him three men who had believed in him and recognised his excellence.

Wahb said: Jibril (peace be upon him) has a station before Allah the Exalted that no other angel has the like of in nearness and excellence. He is the one who receives the Word. When Allah mentions a servant with goodness, Jibril (peace be upon him) receives it, then Mikail (peace be upon him) receives it, then those angels near to them who surround them. When this spreads, they send blessings upon him. Then the angels of the heavens send blessings, then the angels of the earth.

Now Iblis had not been barred from any of the heavens; he would stand in them wherever he wished, and from there he reached Adam (peace be upon him) until he expelled him from the Garden. He continued in this state until Isa (peace be upon him) was raised, and then he was barred from four [heavens]. After that he would ascend only to three, until the time of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), when he was barred from all the heavens except one who steals hearing.

[Wahb] said: Iblis heard the angels responding with blessings upon Ayyub, and envy seized him. He ascended swiftly until he stood at the station in the heaven where he used to stand, and said: "O my Lord, You have bestowed favours upon Your servant Ayyub, and he gave You thanks; You granted him health, and he praised You. Then You did not test him with hardship or affliction. I am a guarantor for You: if You strike him with affliction, he will surely disbelieve in You."

Allah the Exalted said: "Go, for I have given you power over his wealth." The accursed one then swooped down until he reached the earth, gathered the powerful demons (ʿafārīt al-shayāṭīn), and said to them: "What strength do you have, for I have been given power over the wealth of Ayyub?" A demon (ʿifrīt) said: "I have been given such strength that, if I wish, I can turn into a whirlwind of fire, and I will burn everything I reach."

Iblis said: "Then go to the camels and their herdsmen." So he went, and people did not notice until a whirlwind of fire erupted from beneath the earth, and nothing that came near it was spared but was burned. It continued to burn them and their herdsmen until it consumed the last of them.

Iblis then went, in the form of one of those herdsmen, to Ayyub, and found him standing in prayer. When he had finished praying, [Iblis] said: "O Ayyub, do you know what your Lord, whom you have chosen, has done with your camels and their herdsmen?" Ayyub said: "They are His property; He lent them to me, and He has more right to them. When He wishes, He takes them back."

Iblis said: "Your Lord sent down fire from the sky upon them, and they were burned, along with all their herdsmen, and it left the people astonished and bewildered. Some of them say: 'Ayyub was not worshipping anything, and he was only in delusion.' Others say: 'If the god of Ayyub had power over anything, he would have protected his friend.' And yet others say: 'Rather, it is He who did what He did, so that his enemy would rejoice at him and his friend would be grieved by him.'"

Ayyub (peace be upon him) said: "Praise be to Allah, when He gave and when He took away. Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked I shall return to the dust, and naked I shall be gathered to Allah the Exalted. Had Allah known in you, O servant, any good, He would have taken your soul along with those souls, and you would have become a martyr, and He would have rewarded me for you. But Allah knew evil in you, so He delayed you." Then Iblis returned to his companions, humiliated.

Another demon said: "I have such strength that, if I wish, I can let out a cry that no living soul hears without its soul departing." Iblis said: "Then go to the sheep and their shepherds." So he went, cried out at them, and they died, and their shepherd died with them. Then Iblis went out, appearing in the form of the chief of the shepherds, to Ayyub, and said to him the same first words, and Ayyub gave him the same first reply. Iblis returned, disgraced.

Another demon said: "I have such strength that, if I wish, I can become a violent wind that uproots everything I pass over." [Iblis] said: "Then go to the tilled fields and the oxen." So he went and destroyed them. Then Iblis returned in disguise until he came to Ayyub while he was praying, and he said the same as his first words, and Ayyub gave him the same first reply. Iblis then began striking his wealth bit by bit until he had consumed all of it.

When Iblis saw Ayyub's patience in all this, he stood at the station where he used to stand before Allah the Exalted and said: "O my God, will You give me power over his children? For this is a misguiding trial." Allah the Exalted said: "Go, for I have given you power over his children." So he came to Ayyub's children in their palace and kept shaking it from its foundations until he overturned the palace upon them. Then he came to Ayyub in the form of a teacher, while [Ayyub] was wounded, with a split head, his blood and brain flowing, and said: "If only you had seen how your sons were overturned, head down, their brains flowing from their noses, your heart would be torn to pieces." He kept saying this and softening him until Ayyub (peace be upon him) grew tender and wept, and took a handful of dust and placed it on his head. Iblis seized this opportunity. But Ayyub (peace be upon him) did not delay before he sought forgiveness and said "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return."

Iblis ascended and took his station, and said: "O my God, the loss of wealth and children is easy for Ayyub, because he knows You will restore to him his wealth and children. So will You give me power over his body? I am a guarantor for You: if You afflict him in his body, he will surely disbelieve in You." Allah the Exalted said: "Go, for I have given you power over his body, but you have no power over his mind, his heart, or his tongue." The enemy of Allah swooped down swiftly and found Ayyub (peace be upon him) prostrating to Allah the Exalted. He came at him from the direction of the earth, blew a blast into his nostril, and his body was set ablaze; from his head to his feet, boils broke out on him, and an itching seized him that he could not control. He would scratch himself with his nails until his nails fell off, then he rubbed himself with rough woollen cloths, then with pottery and stones, and he kept doing this until his flesh was torn, changed, and gave off a stench.

The people of the village expelled him and placed him on a rubbish heap, and made a shelter for him. Everyone shunned him except his wife, Rahma daughter of Ephraim son of Joseph (peace be upon him), who looked after his affairs.

Then Wahb went on at length in the narrative until he said: Ayyub (peace be upon him) turned to Allah the Exalted, seeking help and humbly supplicating to Him, and said: "O Lord, why did You create me? Would that I had been a menstrual discharge that my mother had cast away! Would that I had known the sin I committed and the deed I did, so that You turned Your noble face away from me! Was I not a home for the stranger, a refuge for the needy, a guardian for the orphan, and a protector for the widow? O my God, I am a humble servant: if I do good, the favour is Yours, and if I do evil, my punishment is in Your hand. You have made me a target for trials and a mark for afflictions, and You have given power over me to that which, if You had given it to a mountain, it would have weakened under its weight. O my God, my fingers have been cut off, my molars have fallen out, my hair has scattered, my wealth has gone, and I have come to beg for a morsel, and [those] who give it to me do so with a reproach, taunting me with my poverty and the destruction of my children."

Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Ansari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among the sentences in this speech is: "Would that You had disliked me and not created me." Then he said: If this were correct, Iblis would have seized upon it, for his aim is to lead him to complaint and to remove him from the adornment of the patient. Allah the Exalted did not report of him anything except his saying: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant. Indeed, he was ever turning back [to Allah].﴾ [Qur'an 38:44]. The scholars differed concerning the cause for which he said: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful,﴾ and concerning the duration of his affliction.

**The first narration:** Ibn Shihab narrated from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ayyub (peace be upon him) remained in affliction for eighteen years. Both the near and the distant abandoned him, except two men among his brothers who would come to him in the morning and evening. One of them said to the other one day: 'By Allah, Ayyub has committed a sin that no one in the worlds has committed.' His companion said: 'And what is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah the Exalted has not shown him mercy or removed what afflicts him.' When they came to Ayyub, the man could not restrain himself and mentioned this to Ayyub (peace be upon him). Ayyub said: 'I do not know what you are saying, except that Allah the Exalted knows that I used to pass by two men quarrelling and remembering Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and I would return to my house and atone on their behalf, out of dislike that Allah be mentioned except for a right purpose.'"

In another narration: "When the two men entered upon him, they noticed a foul smell, and they said: 'If Ayyub had any good with Allah, he would not have reached this state.' Nothing distressed Ayyub more of what he was tested with than what he heard from them. So he said: 'O Allah, if You know that I have never gone to sleep full while I knew of a hungry person, then testify to me.' And He testified to him while they were listening. Then Ayyub (peace be upon him) fell prostrate and said: 'O Allah, I will not raise my head until You remove what is upon me.' So Allah removed what was upon him."

**The second narration:** Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Ayyub (peace be upon him) remained, after he was cast onto the rubbish heap, for seven years and some months. No wealth, child, or friend remained for him except his wife Rahma, who bore [it] patiently with him. She would bring him food and praise Allah the Exalted together with Ayyub. Ayyub was constant in praising Allah the Exalted, extolling Him, and being patient with what He had tested him with. Then Iblis let out a cry out of distress at Ayyub's patience, and his troops gathered from the corners of the earth and said to him: 'What is your news?' He said: 'This servant has defeated me, the one whom I asked Allah to give me power over, along with his wealth and children. I left him with no wealth or child, and he only increased in patience and praise of Allah the Exalted. Then I was given power over his body, and I left him lying on a rubbish heap, and no one approaches him except his wife. Yet he does not cease from remembrance and praise of Allah. So I have sought your help that you may assist me against him.' They said to him: 'Where is your cunning? Where is your work by which you destroyed those who passed before?' He said: 'All of that has been nullified in [the case of] Ayyub, so advise me.' They said: 'How did you lead Adam astray when you expelled him from the Garden?' He said: 'Through his wife.' They said:

[Page 179]

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 83–84 (part 2 of 3):

So [it was said to him], "Your claim concerning Job is from [the side of] his wife, for he cannot disobey her, since no one approaches him except her." He said, "You are right." So he set out until he came to his wife, and he appeared to her in the form of a man. He said, "Where is your husband, O servant of God?" She said, "He is here, scratching his sores, and the worms are moving about in his body." When he heard her, he hoped that all of this was [only] impatience, so he whispered to her and reminded her of the blessings and wealth she had had, and reminded her of Job's beauty and youth. [Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said:] Then she cried out, and when she cried out, he knew that she had become impatient. So he brought her a young goat and said, "Let Job slaughter this for me, and he will be healed." He said: So she came crying out to Job, "O Job, how long will your Lord torment you? Will He not have mercy on you? Where is the wealth? Where are the livestock? Where are the children? Where is the friend? Where is the good complexion? Where is your body, which has decayed and become like ashes, and in which the worms move about? Slaughter this young goat and find rest."

Job, peace be upon him, said, "The enemy of God has come to you and blew into you, and you responded to him! Woe to you! Do you see what you are weeping over, of what you mention from what we had of wealth, children and health? Who gave us that?" She said, "God." He said, "For how long did He let us enjoy it?" She said, "Eighty years." He said, "And since when has God tested us with this affliction?" She said, "For seven years and several months." He said, "Woe to you! By God, you have not been fair to your Lord. Could you not have been patient in affliction for eighty years, as we were in ease for eighty years? By God, if God heals me, I will flog you a hundred lashes. You commanded me to slaughter for other than God, and it is forbidden for me to taste, after this, any of the food and drink you bring me." So he drove her away, and she left. When Job considered his situation, having no food, no drink, and no friend, and his wife having gone, he fell down prostrate and said: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾. Then it was said to him: "Raise your head, for We have answered you." ﴿Strike with your foot﴾ [Sad 38:42]. So he struck with his foot, and a spring of water gushed forth, and he bathed in it, and every creature on the outer surface of his body fell off. Then he struck with his foot a second time, and another spring gushed forth, and he drank from it, and every disease in his interior came out. He stood up healthy, his youth and beauty returned to him until he became more beautiful than he had ever been. Then he was clothed in a robe. When he stood up, he began to look around and saw nothing of what he had had of family, children and wealth except that God, exalted is He, had multiplied it, until it became better than it had been. It is related that the water in which he had bathed scattered over his chest as locusts of gold.

He began to gather it in his hands, and God revealed to him: "O Job, have I not made you rich?" He said, "Yes, but it is Your blessing, and who could be satisfied with it?" Then he went out and sat down in an elevated place. Then his wife said, "Suppose he drove me away; shall I leave him until he dies of hunger and the beasts eat him? I will return to him." When she returned, she did not see that dunghill or that condition, and behold, the affairs had changed. So she began to wander about where the dunghill had been, weeping, and that was in the sight of Job, peace be upon him. She feared approaching the owner of the robe and asking him about him, so Job, peace be upon him, sent for her and called her and said, "What do you want, O servant of God?" She wept and said, "I wanted that afflicted one who was lying on the dunghill." Job, peace be upon him, said to her, "What became of him?" She wept and said, "My husband." He said, "Would you recognize him if you saw him?" She said, "Could anyone who sees him fail to recognize him!" He smiled and said, "I am he." So she recognized him by his laughter, and she embraced him. Then he said, "You commanded me to slaughter a young goat for Iblis, and I obeyed God and disobeyed the Devil, and I called upon God, exalted is He, and He returned to me what you see."

The third narration: al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: He remained in the affliction for seven years, seven months, seven days and seven hours. Wahb, may God have mercy on him, said: He remained in the affliction for three years. When Job overcame Iblis, may God curse him, Iblis went to his wife in a form unlike the form of the children of Adam in size and beauty, upon a mount unlike the mounts of people, and said to her, "Are you the companion of Job?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Do you know me?" She said, "No." He said, "I am the god of the earth. I am the one who did to Job what I did, because he worshipped the God of the heavens and left me, and so angered me. If he would prostrate to me one prostration, I would return to you and to him all of your wealth and children, for that is in my hand." Wahb said: I heard that he also said, "If your companion had eaten food without mentioning God, exalted is He, he would have been healed of what he is in," [and] in another narration: "Rather, he said to her, 'If you wish, prostrate to me one prostration, so that I may return to you the wealth and the children and heal your husband.'" So she returned to Job and informed him of what he had said to her. Job said to her, "The enemy of God has come to you to tempt you away from your religion." Then he swore that if God healed him, he would flog her a hundred lashes. At that point he said: ﴿harm has touched me﴾, meaning, from the hope of Iblis for my prostration to him, and the prostration of my wife to him, and his calling her and me to disbelief.

The fourth narration: Wahb said: Job's wife, peace be upon him, used to work for people and bring him his sustenance. When the affliction lengthened upon him, people grew weary of her, and they did not employ her. One day she sought some food and found nothing, so she cut off a lock of her hair and sold it for a loaf of bread. She brought it to him, and he said to her, "Where is your lock?" She informed him of that, and then he said: ﴿harm has touched me﴾.

The fifth narration: Isma'il al-Suddi said: Job did not say ﴿harm has touched me﴾ except for three things:
The first: the saying of the two men to him, "If your deeds which we used to see were for God, the Exalted, then what has befallen you would not have befallen you."
The second: his wife had three locks of hair, and she deliberately cut one of them and sold it, and they gave her bread and meat for it. She came to Job, peace be upon him, and he said, "From where is this?" She said, "Eat, for it is lawful." When the next day came, she found nothing, so she sold the second, and likewise on the third day, and she said, "Eat, for it is lawful." He said, "I will not eat what you do not inform me of." So she informed him, and that reached Job to a degree that only God knows. It was said: She only sold her locks because Iblis had appeared to a people in the form of a human being and said, "If you leave Job in your town, I fear that what he has of the illness will spread to you." So they expelled him to the gate of the town. Then he said to them, "His wife enters your houses and works and touches her husband. Do you not fear that his illness will spread to you?" At that point no one employed her, so she sold her braid.
The third: when his wife said to him what she said, then he supplicated.

The sixth narration: It was said: a worm fell from his thigh, so he picked it up and returned it to its place, and said, "God, exalted is He, has made me a provision for you." Then it bit him a severe bite, and he said: ﴿harm has touched me﴾. God, exalted is He, revealed to him: "Had I not placed beneath every hair of yours patience, you would not have been patient."

* * *

The second issue: The Mu'tazilah have criticized this story on several grounds.
The first: al-Jubba'i said: Some ignoramuses have claimed that the sickness he had was an act of the Devil, whom God had empowered over him, because of His saying, exalted is He, quoting him: ﴿The Devil has touched me with fatigue and torment﴾ [Sad 38:41]. This is ignorance. Firstly, because if he were able to produce diseases and illnesses and their opposite, health, then it would be possible for him to create bodies, and whoever is in this condition would be a god. Secondly, because God, exalted is He, informed about him and his armies that he said: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22], and what must be affirmed is the report of God, exalted is He, not reliance on what is narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih, may God be pleased with him.

Know that this objection is weak, because what is mentioned in the story is that the Devil blew into his nostril, and the itching occurred in him. Why do you say that whoever is capable of a blowing that produces such itching must be capable of creating bodies? Is this not pure arbitrary assertion? As for relying on the text, it is weak, because he only undertakes this act when he knows that, if he undertook it, God would not prevent him from it. This condition only arose in the case of Job, peace be upon him, according to what the story indicates, that he asked God's permission and He granted him permission for it. And when that is so, there remains no contradiction between that text and this story.

The second: They said: What is narrated, that he, peace be upon him, asked only at specific times, is far-fetched, because it is established by reason that it is good for a person to ask his Lord in such matters and to seek refuge in Him, just as it is good for him to seek treatment. And if it is permissible for him to ask his Lord at a time of grief over what he sees of his brothers and family, it is also permissible for him to ask his Lord on his own behalf.

If it is said: Is it not possible that He, exalted is He, imposed upon him as a worship that he should not ask for relief except at the end of his affair? We reply: That is possible, by informing him that the sending of that upon him for a specific period is necessarily one of his interests and the interests of others. So he, peace be upon him, knew that there was no justification for asking about this particular matter. When the time drew near, it became permissible for him to ask for it, since it is permissible for it to last, and it is permissible for it to end.

The third: They said: It is not permissible that the sickness reached the degree of repelling people from him, because sicknesses that repel from acceptance are not permissible for the prophets, peace be upon them. This is the total of what has been said regarding this story.

* * *

The third issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that harm has touched me﴾, means: he called out, "Indeed, harm has touched me." It is recited ﴿Inni﴾ with a kasra, on the assumption of an implied verb of saying, or because the call includes the meaning of speech. And ﴿al-Durr﴾ with a fatha means harm in everything, and with a damma means harm in the self, from sickness and emaciation.

The fourth issue: He, peace be upon him, was gentle in his request, in that he mentioned himself with what calls for mercy, and he mentioned his Lord with the utmost mercy, and he did not state the desired matter explicitly. If it is said: Does complaining not detract from his being patient? The answer: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, may God have mercy on him, said: Whoever complains to God, exalted is He, that is not counted as impatience if, in his complaint, he is content with God's decree, since it is not a condition of patience to find affliction sweet. Did you not hear the saying of Ya'qub, peace be upon him: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my sorrow to God﴾ [Yusuf 12:86]? As for his saying: ﴿and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, the evidence that He, glorified is He, is ﴿the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ consists of several matters:
The first: that everyone who shows mercy to another either does so seeking praise in this world, or reward in the Hereafter, or to dispel natural tenderness from the temperament, and in that case the aim of that merciful one is the benefit of his own self. But the Truthful One, glorified is He, shows mercy to His servants without any of these aspects, and without any increase or decrease reaching Him from that mercy in praise or in attributes of perfection. Therefore He, glorified is He, is the Most Merciful of the merciful.
The second: that everyone who shows mercy to another does not do so except by the help of God's mercy, exalted is He. For whoever gives another food or clothing, or averts an affliction from him, if He, glorified is He, had not created the food, the clothing, the medicines and the nourishments, no one could have given that thing. Then, after that gift reaches him, if He, glorified is He, had not made it a means of comfort, no benefit would have been gained from it. Thus the mercy of the servants is preceded by the mercy of God, exalted is He, and followed by His mercy. Indeed, their mercy, between the two extremes, is like a drop in the sea. Therefore it is necessary that He, exalted is He, be the Most Merciful of the merciful.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 83–84 (part 3 of 3):

Third: If God, exalted is He, had not created in the servant's heart those motives and desires, the occurrence of that act from him would have been impossible. Thus the One who is truly Merciful is God, glorified is He, inasmuch as He is the One who brought into being that motive. It is established, then, that He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. If it is said: How can He be the Most Merciful of the merciful, when He, glorified is He, filled the world with calamities, diseases, sicknesses and pains, and gave some power over others so that they slaughter, break and harm one another, while He was able to spare each one from causing pain and harm to the other? The answer: His being harmful does not contradict His being beneficial; rather He is the Harmful and the Beneficial. His harming is not to repel a hardship, and His benefiting is not to bring about a benefit. Rather, "He is not questioned about what He does" (Qur'an 21:23).

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We responded to him﴾, it indicates that he supplicated his Lord. However, this supplication may have been made by him in the form of an indirect allusion (ta'rid), as one says: "If you see, or want, or love, then do such-and-such." It may also have been an explicit supplication. Although the first is more fitting to good manners and to the indication of the verse, then, God, glorified is He, made clear that He removed from him the harm he had, and this requires restoring to him what had been in his body and his circumstances. God, exalted is He, stated that He gave him his family, and this includes whoever is attributed to him among wife, children and others.

Then there are two views concerning this:

The first, which is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Kalbi and Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with them, is that God, exalted is He, revived for him his family, meaning his children, in their own persons.

The second: al-Layth, may Allah be pleased with him, related that he said: Mujahid sent to Ikrimah and asked him about the verse. He said: It was said to him: "Your family is for you in the Hereafter. If you wish, We will hasten them for you in this world; and if you wish, they will be for you in the Hereafter and We will give you the like of them in this world." He said: "They will be mine in the Hereafter, and I will be given the like of them in this world."

The first view is preferable, because His saying, ﴿And We gave him his family﴾, indicates by its apparent meaning that God, exalted is He, restored them in this world, and gave him along with them the like of them as well.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a reminder for the worshippers﴾, it indicates that God, exalted is He, did this so that they would reflect upon it, and so that it would be a motive for the worshippers toward patience and seeking reward (ihtisab). He specified the worshippers for mention [ ى ] because they are the ones who especially benefit from this.

[Page 177]

**The Sixth Story: The Story of Ayyub (peace be upon him)**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Ayyub, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."﴾ ﴿So We answered him and removed what was upon him of harm, and We gave him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.﴾

Know that in the matter of Ayyub (peace be upon him), and in what Allah the Exalted mentions of his circumstances here and elsewhere in the Qur'an, there are lessons and proofs that are not found elsewhere. This is because Allah the Exalted, despite His great favour toward him, sent upon him a severe illness of the kind He had not sent upon anyone else, and [this was] to make it known to him, to others, and to everyone who heard of it, that this world is the field of the Hereafter, and that it is obligatory upon a person to be patient with the trials he encounters in it, to strive in discharging the right of Allah the Exalted, and to be patient in both states of adversity and ease. There are several issues concerning this:

**The first issue:** Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Ayyub (peace be upon him) was a man from the Romans. He was Ayyub ibn Anus, and he was from the descendants of Esau ibn Isaac, and his mother was from the descendants of Lot. Allah the Exalted had chosen him and made him a prophet. Along with this, He had given him a generous share of the world's bounties: livestock, gardens, and blessings, and He gave him a household and children, both sons and daughters. He was merciful to the needy, he would look after orphans and widows, and he would honour guests. He had with him three men who had believed in him and recognised his excellence.

Wahb said: Jibril (peace be upon him) has a station before Allah the Exalted that no other angel has the like of in nearness and excellence. He is the one who receives the Word. When Allah mentions a servant with goodness, Jibril (peace be upon him) receives it, then Mikail (peace be upon him) receives it, then those angels near to them who surround them. When this spreads, they send blessings upon him. Then the angels of the heavens send blessings, then the angels of the earth.

Now Iblis had not been barred from any of the heavens; he would stand in them wherever he wished, and from there he reached Adam (peace be upon him) until he expelled him from the Garden. He continued in this state until Isa (peace be upon him) was raised, and then he was barred from four [heavens]. After that he would ascend only to three, until the time of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), when he was barred from all the heavens except one who steals hearing.

[Wahb] said: Iblis heard the angels responding with blessings upon Ayyub, and envy seized him. He ascended swiftly until he stood at the station in the heaven where he used to stand, and said: "O my Lord, You have bestowed favours upon Your servant Ayyub, and he gave You thanks; You granted him health, and he praised You. Then You did not test him with hardship or affliction. I am a guarantor for You: if You strike him with affliction, he will surely disbelieve in You."

Allah the Exalted said: "Go, for I have given you power over his wealth." The accursed one then swooped down until he reached the earth, gathered the powerful demons (ʿafārīt al-shayāṭīn), and said to them: "What strength do you have, for I have been given power over the wealth of Ayyub?" A demon (ʿifrīt) said: "I have been given such strength that, if I wish, I can turn into a whirlwind of fire, and I will burn everything I reach."

Iblis said: "Then go to the camels and their herdsmen." So he went, and people did not notice until a whirlwind of fire erupted from beneath the earth, and nothing that came near it was spared but was burned. It continued to burn them and their herdsmen until it consumed the last of them.

Iblis then went, in the form of one of those herdsmen, to Ayyub, and found him standing in prayer. When he had finished praying, [Iblis] said: "O Ayyub, do you know what your Lord, whom you have chosen, has done with your camels and their herdsmen?" Ayyub said: "They are His property; He lent them to me, and He has more right to them. When He wishes, He takes them back."

Iblis said: "Your Lord sent down fire from the sky upon them, and they were burned, along with all their herdsmen, and it left the people astonished and bewildered. Some of them say: 'Ayyub was not worshipping anything, and he was only in delusion.' Others say: 'If the god of Ayyub had power over anything, he would have protected his friend.' And yet others say: 'Rather, it is He who did what He did, so that his enemy would rejoice at him and his friend would be grieved by him.'"

Ayyub (peace be upon him) said: "Praise be to Allah, when He gave and when He took away. Naked I came out of my mother's womb, and naked I shall return to the dust, and naked I shall be gathered to Allah the Exalted. Had Allah known in you, O servant, any good, He would have taken your soul along with those souls, and you would have become a martyr, and He would have rewarded me for you. But Allah knew evil in you, so He delayed you." Then Iblis returned to his companions, humiliated.

Another demon said: "I have such strength that, if I wish, I can let out a cry that no living soul hears without its soul departing." Iblis said: "Then go to the sheep and their shepherds." So he went, cried out at them, and they died, and their shepherd died with them. Then Iblis went out, appearing in the form of the chief of the shepherds, to Ayyub, and said to him the same first words, and Ayyub gave him the same first reply. Iblis returned, disgraced.

Another demon said: "I have such strength that, if I wish, I can become a violent wind that uproots everything I pass over." [Iblis] said: "Then go to the tilled fields and the oxen." So he went and destroyed them. Then Iblis returned in disguise until he came to Ayyub while he was praying, and he said the same as his first words, and Ayyub gave him the same first reply. Iblis then began striking his wealth bit by bit until he had consumed all of it.

When Iblis saw Ayyub's patience in all this, he stood at the station where he used to stand before Allah the Exalted and said: "O my God, will You give me power over his children? For this is a misguiding trial." Allah the Exalted said: "Go, for I have given you power over his children." So he came to Ayyub's children in their palace and kept shaking it from its foundations until he overturned the palace upon them. Then he came to Ayyub in the form of a teacher, while [Ayyub] was wounded, with a split head, his blood and brain flowing, and said: "If only you had seen how your sons were overturned, head down, their brains flowing from their noses, your heart would be torn to pieces." He kept saying this and softening him until Ayyub (peace be upon him) grew tender and wept, and took a handful of dust and placed it on his head. Iblis seized this opportunity. But Ayyub (peace be upon him) did not delay before he sought forgiveness and said "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return."

Iblis ascended and took his station, and said: "O my God, the loss of wealth and children is easy for Ayyub, because he knows You will restore to him his wealth and children. So will You give me power over his body? I am a guarantor for You: if You afflict him in his body, he will surely disbelieve in You." Allah the Exalted said: "Go, for I have given you power over his body, but you have no power over his mind, his heart, or his tongue." The enemy of Allah swooped down swiftly and found Ayyub (peace be upon him) prostrating to Allah the Exalted. He came at him from the direction of the earth, blew a blast into his nostril, and his body was set ablaze; from his head to his feet, boils broke out on him, and an itching seized him that he could not control. He would scratch himself with his nails until his nails fell off, then he rubbed himself with rough woollen cloths, then with pottery and stones, and he kept doing this until his flesh was torn, changed, and gave off a stench.

The people of the village expelled him and placed him on a rubbish heap, and made a shelter for him. Everyone shunned him except his wife, Rahma daughter of Ephraim son of Joseph (peace be upon him), who looked after his affairs.

Then Wahb went on at length in the narrative until he said: Ayyub (peace be upon him) turned to Allah the Exalted, seeking help and humbly supplicating to Him, and said: "O Lord, why did You create me? Would that I had been a menstrual discharge that my mother had cast away! Would that I had known the sin I committed and the deed I did, so that You turned Your noble face away from me! Was I not a home for the stranger, a refuge for the needy, a guardian for the orphan, and a protector for the widow? O my God, I am a humble servant: if I do good, the favour is Yours, and if I do evil, my punishment is in Your hand. You have made me a target for trials and a mark for afflictions, and You have given power over me to that which, if You had given it to a mountain, it would have weakened under its weight. O my God, my fingers have been cut off, my molars have fallen out, my hair has scattered, my wealth has gone, and I have come to beg for a morsel, and [those] who give it to me do so with a reproach, taunting me with my poverty and the destruction of my children."

Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Ansari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among the sentences in this speech is: "Would that You had disliked me and not created me." Then he said: If this were correct, Iblis would have seized upon it, for his aim is to lead him to complaint and to remove him from the adornment of the patient. Allah the Exalted did not report of him anything except his saying: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾ Then He said: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient; an excellent servant. Indeed, he was ever turning back [to Allah].﴾ [Qur'an 38:44]. The scholars differed concerning the cause for which he said: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful,﴾ and concerning the duration of his affliction.

**The first narration:** Ibn Shihab narrated from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ayyub (peace be upon him) remained in affliction for eighteen years. Both the near and the distant abandoned him, except two men among his brothers who would come to him in the morning and evening. One of them said to the other one day: 'By Allah, Ayyub has committed a sin that no one in the worlds has committed.' His companion said: 'And what is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah the Exalted has not shown him mercy or removed what afflicts him.' When they came to Ayyub, the man could not restrain himself and mentioned this to Ayyub (peace be upon him). Ayyub said: 'I do not know what you are saying, except that Allah the Exalted knows that I used to pass by two men quarrelling and remembering Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and I would return to my house and atone on their behalf, out of dislike that Allah be mentioned except for a right purpose.'"

In another narration: "When the two men entered upon him, they noticed a foul smell, and they said: 'If Ayyub had any good with Allah, he would not have reached this state.' Nothing distressed Ayyub more of what he was tested with than what he heard from them. So he said: 'O Allah, if You know that I have never gone to sleep full while I knew of a hungry person, then testify to me.' And He testified to him while they were listening. Then Ayyub (peace be upon him) fell prostrate and said: 'O Allah, I will not raise my head until You remove what is upon me.' So Allah removed what was upon him."

**The second narration:** Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Ayyub (peace be upon him) remained, after he was cast onto the rubbish heap, for seven years and some months. No wealth, child, or friend remained for him except his wife Rahma, who bore [it] patiently with him. She would bring him food and praise Allah the Exalted together with Ayyub. Ayyub was constant in praising Allah the Exalted, extolling Him, and being patient with what He had tested him with. Then Iblis let out a cry out of distress at Ayyub's patience, and his troops gathered from the corners of the earth and said to him: 'What is your news?' He said: 'This servant has defeated me, the one whom I asked Allah to give me power over, along with his wealth and children. I left him with no wealth or child, and he only increased in patience and praise of Allah the Exalted. Then I was given power over his body, and I left him lying on a rubbish heap, and no one approaches him except his wife. Yet he does not cease from remembrance and praise of Allah. So I have sought your help that you may assist me against him.' They said to him: 'Where is your cunning? Where is your work by which you destroyed those who passed before?' He said: 'All of that has been nullified in [the case of] Ayyub, so advise me.' They said: 'How did you lead Adam astray when you expelled him from the Garden?' He said: 'Through his wife.' They said:

[Page 179]

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 83–84 (part 2 of 3):

So [it was said to him], "Your claim concerning Job is from [the side of] his wife, for he cannot disobey her, since no one approaches him except her." He said, "You are right." So he set out until he came to his wife, and he appeared to her in the form of a man. He said, "Where is your husband, O servant of God?" She said, "He is here, scratching his sores, and the worms are moving about in his body." When he heard her, he hoped that all of this was [only] impatience, so he whispered to her and reminded her of the blessings and wealth she had had, and reminded her of Job's beauty and youth. [Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said:] Then she cried out, and when she cried out, he knew that she had become impatient. So he brought her a young goat and said, "Let Job slaughter this for me, and he will be healed." He said: So she came crying out to Job, "O Job, how long will your Lord torment you? Will He not have mercy on you? Where is the wealth? Where are the livestock? Where are the children? Where is the friend? Where is the good complexion? Where is your body, which has decayed and become like ashes, and in which the worms move about? Slaughter this young goat and find rest."

Job, peace be upon him, said, "The enemy of God has come to you and blew into you, and you responded to him! Woe to you! Do you see what you are weeping over, of what you mention from what we had of wealth, children and health? Who gave us that?" She said, "God." He said, "For how long did He let us enjoy it?" She said, "Eighty years." He said, "And since when has God tested us with this affliction?" She said, "For seven years and several months." He said, "Woe to you! By God, you have not been fair to your Lord. Could you not have been patient in affliction for eighty years, as we were in ease for eighty years? By God, if God heals me, I will flog you a hundred lashes. You commanded me to slaughter for other than God, and it is forbidden for me to taste, after this, any of the food and drink you bring me." So he drove her away, and she left. When Job considered his situation, having no food, no drink, and no friend, and his wife having gone, he fell down prostrate and said: ﴿Indeed, harm has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾. Then it was said to him: "Raise your head, for We have answered you." ﴿Strike with your foot﴾ [Sad 38:42]. So he struck with his foot, and a spring of water gushed forth, and he bathed in it, and every creature on the outer surface of his body fell off. Then he struck with his foot a second time, and another spring gushed forth, and he drank from it, and every disease in his interior came out. He stood up healthy, his youth and beauty returned to him until he became more beautiful than he had ever been. Then he was clothed in a robe. When he stood up, he began to look around and saw nothing of what he had had of family, children and wealth except that God, exalted is He, had multiplied it, until it became better than it had been. It is related that the water in which he had bathed scattered over his chest as locusts of gold.

He began to gather it in his hands, and God revealed to him: "O Job, have I not made you rich?" He said, "Yes, but it is Your blessing, and who could be satisfied with it?" Then he went out and sat down in an elevated place. Then his wife said, "Suppose he drove me away; shall I leave him until he dies of hunger and the beasts eat him? I will return to him." When she returned, she did not see that dunghill or that condition, and behold, the affairs had changed. So she began to wander about where the dunghill had been, weeping, and that was in the sight of Job, peace be upon him. She feared approaching the owner of the robe and asking him about him, so Job, peace be upon him, sent for her and called her and said, "What do you want, O servant of God?" She wept and said, "I wanted that afflicted one who was lying on the dunghill." Job, peace be upon him, said to her, "What became of him?" She wept and said, "My husband." He said, "Would you recognize him if you saw him?" She said, "Could anyone who sees him fail to recognize him!" He smiled and said, "I am he." So she recognized him by his laughter, and she embraced him. Then he said, "You commanded me to slaughter a young goat for Iblis, and I obeyed God and disobeyed the Devil, and I called upon God, exalted is He, and He returned to me what you see."

The third narration: al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: He remained in the affliction for seven years, seven months, seven days and seven hours. Wahb, may God have mercy on him, said: He remained in the affliction for three years. When Job overcame Iblis, may God curse him, Iblis went to his wife in a form unlike the form of the children of Adam in size and beauty, upon a mount unlike the mounts of people, and said to her, "Are you the companion of Job?" She said, "Yes." He said, "Do you know me?" She said, "No." He said, "I am the god of the earth. I am the one who did to Job what I did, because he worshipped the God of the heavens and left me, and so angered me. If he would prostrate to me one prostration, I would return to you and to him all of your wealth and children, for that is in my hand." Wahb said: I heard that he also said, "If your companion had eaten food without mentioning God, exalted is He, he would have been healed of what he is in," [and] in another narration: "Rather, he said to her, 'If you wish, prostrate to me one prostration, so that I may return to you the wealth and the children and heal your husband.'" So she returned to Job and informed him of what he had said to her. Job said to her, "The enemy of God has come to you to tempt you away from your religion." Then he swore that if God healed him, he would flog her a hundred lashes. At that point he said: ﴿harm has touched me﴾, meaning, from the hope of Iblis for my prostration to him, and the prostration of my wife to him, and his calling her and me to disbelief.

The fourth narration: Wahb said: Job's wife, peace be upon him, used to work for people and bring him his sustenance. When the affliction lengthened upon him, people grew weary of her, and they did not employ her. One day she sought some food and found nothing, so she cut off a lock of her hair and sold it for a loaf of bread. She brought it to him, and he said to her, "Where is your lock?" She informed him of that, and then he said: ﴿harm has touched me﴾.

The fifth narration: Isma'il al-Suddi said: Job did not say ﴿harm has touched me﴾ except for three things:
The first: the saying of the two men to him, "If your deeds which we used to see were for God, the Exalted, then what has befallen you would not have befallen you."
The second: his wife had three locks of hair, and she deliberately cut one of them and sold it, and they gave her bread and meat for it. She came to Job, peace be upon him, and he said, "From where is this?" She said, "Eat, for it is lawful." When the next day came, she found nothing, so she sold the second, and likewise on the third day, and she said, "Eat, for it is lawful." He said, "I will not eat what you do not inform me of." So she informed him, and that reached Job to a degree that only God knows. It was said: She only sold her locks because Iblis had appeared to a people in the form of a human being and said, "If you leave Job in your town, I fear that what he has of the illness will spread to you." So they expelled him to the gate of the town. Then he said to them, "His wife enters your houses and works and touches her husband. Do you not fear that his illness will spread to you?" At that point no one employed her, so she sold her braid.
The third: when his wife said to him what she said, then he supplicated.

The sixth narration: It was said: a worm fell from his thigh, so he picked it up and returned it to its place, and said, "God, exalted is He, has made me a provision for you." Then it bit him a severe bite, and he said: ﴿harm has touched me﴾. God, exalted is He, revealed to him: "Had I not placed beneath every hair of yours patience, you would not have been patient."

* * *

The second issue: The Mu'tazilah have criticized this story on several grounds.
The first: al-Jubba'i said: Some ignoramuses have claimed that the sickness he had was an act of the Devil, whom God had empowered over him, because of His saying, exalted is He, quoting him: ﴿The Devil has touched me with fatigue and torment﴾ [Sad 38:41]. This is ignorance. Firstly, because if he were able to produce diseases and illnesses and their opposite, health, then it would be possible for him to create bodies, and whoever is in this condition would be a god. Secondly, because God, exalted is He, informed about him and his armies that he said: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22], and what must be affirmed is the report of God, exalted is He, not reliance on what is narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih, may God be pleased with him.

Know that this objection is weak, because what is mentioned in the story is that the Devil blew into his nostril, and the itching occurred in him. Why do you say that whoever is capable of a blowing that produces such itching must be capable of creating bodies? Is this not pure arbitrary assertion? As for relying on the text, it is weak, because he only undertakes this act when he knows that, if he undertook it, God would not prevent him from it. This condition only arose in the case of Job, peace be upon him, according to what the story indicates, that he asked God's permission and He granted him permission for it. And when that is so, there remains no contradiction between that text and this story.

The second: They said: What is narrated, that he, peace be upon him, asked only at specific times, is far-fetched, because it is established by reason that it is good for a person to ask his Lord in such matters and to seek refuge in Him, just as it is good for him to seek treatment. And if it is permissible for him to ask his Lord at a time of grief over what he sees of his brothers and family, it is also permissible for him to ask his Lord on his own behalf.

If it is said: Is it not possible that He, exalted is He, imposed upon him as a worship that he should not ask for relief except at the end of his affair? We reply: That is possible, by informing him that the sending of that upon him for a specific period is necessarily one of his interests and the interests of others. So he, peace be upon him, knew that there was no justification for asking about this particular matter. When the time drew near, it became permissible for him to ask for it, since it is permissible for it to last, and it is permissible for it to end.

The third: They said: It is not permissible that the sickness reached the degree of repelling people from him, because sicknesses that repel from acceptance are not permissible for the prophets, peace be upon them. This is the total of what has been said regarding this story.

* * *

The third issue: The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that harm has touched me﴾, means: he called out, "Indeed, harm has touched me." It is recited ﴿Inni﴾ with a kasra, on the assumption of an implied verb of saying, or because the call includes the meaning of speech. And ﴿al-Durr﴾ with a fatha means harm in everything, and with a damma means harm in the self, from sickness and emaciation.

The fourth issue: He, peace be upon him, was gentle in his request, in that he mentioned himself with what calls for mercy, and he mentioned his Lord with the utmost mercy, and he did not state the desired matter explicitly. If it is said: Does complaining not detract from his being patient? The answer: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, may God have mercy on him, said: Whoever complains to God, exalted is He, that is not counted as impatience if, in his complaint, he is content with God's decree, since it is not a condition of patience to find affliction sweet. Did you not hear the saying of Ya'qub, peace be upon him: ﴿I only complain of my anguish and my sorrow to God﴾ [Yusuf 12:86]? As for his saying: ﴿and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, the evidence that He, glorified is He, is ﴿the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾ consists of several matters:
The first: that everyone who shows mercy to another either does so seeking praise in this world, or reward in the Hereafter, or to dispel natural tenderness from the temperament, and in that case the aim of that merciful one is the benefit of his own self. But the Truthful One, glorified is He, shows mercy to His servants without any of these aspects, and without any increase or decrease reaching Him from that mercy in praise or in attributes of perfection. Therefore He, glorified is He, is the Most Merciful of the merciful.
The second: that everyone who shows mercy to another does not do so except by the help of God's mercy, exalted is He. For whoever gives another food or clothing, or averts an affliction from him, if He, glorified is He, had not created the food, the clothing, the medicines and the nourishments, no one could have given that thing. Then, after that gift reaches him, if He, glorified is He, had not made it a means of comfort, no benefit would have been gained from it. Thus the mercy of the servants is preceded by the mercy of God, exalted is He, and followed by His mercy. Indeed, their mercy, between the two extremes, is like a drop in the sea. Therefore it is necessary that He, exalted is He, be the Most Merciful of the merciful.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 83–84 (part 3 of 3):

Third: If God, exalted is He, had not created in the servant's heart those motives and desires, the occurrence of that act from him would have been impossible. Thus the One who is truly Merciful is God, glorified is He, inasmuch as He is the One who brought into being that motive. It is established, then, that He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. If it is said: How can He be the Most Merciful of the merciful, when He, glorified is He, filled the world with calamities, diseases, sicknesses and pains, and gave some power over others so that they slaughter, break and harm one another, while He was able to spare each one from causing pain and harm to the other? The answer: His being harmful does not contradict His being beneficial; rather He is the Harmful and the Beneficial. His harming is not to repel a hardship, and His benefiting is not to bring about a benefit. Rather, "He is not questioned about what He does" (Qur'an 21:23).

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We responded to him﴾, it indicates that he supplicated his Lord. However, this supplication may have been made by him in the form of an indirect allusion (ta'rid), as one says: "If you see, or want, or love, then do such-and-such." It may also have been an explicit supplication. Although the first is more fitting to good manners and to the indication of the verse, then, God, glorified is He, made clear that He removed from him the harm he had, and this requires restoring to him what had been in his body and his circumstances. God, exalted is He, stated that He gave him his family, and this includes whoever is attributed to him among wife, children and others.

Then there are two views concerning this:

The first, which is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Muqatil, al-Kalbi and Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with them, is that God, exalted is He, revived for him his family, meaning his children, in their own persons.

The second: al-Layth, may Allah be pleased with him, related that he said: Mujahid sent to Ikrimah and asked him about the verse. He said: It was said to him: "Your family is for you in the Hereafter. If you wish, We will hasten them for you in this world; and if you wish, they will be for you in the Hereafter and We will give you the like of them in this world." He said: "They will be mine in the Hereafter, and I will be given the like of them in this world."

The first view is preferable, because His saying, ﴿And We gave him his family﴾, indicates by its apparent meaning that God, exalted is He, restored them in this world, and gave him along with them the like of them as well.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a reminder for the worshippers﴾, it indicates that God, exalted is He, did this so that they would reflect upon it, and so that it would be a motive for the worshippers toward patience and seeking reward (ihtisab). He specified the worshippers for mention [ ى ] because they are the ones who especially benefit from this.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 85–86:

[The Seventh Story]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Ishmael, and Idris, and Dhu al-Kifl; each of them was among the patient.﴾ ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed they were among the righteous.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the patience of Ayyub (peace be upon him) and his turning wholly to Him, He followed it with mention of these, for they too were among those who were patient in the face of hardships, trials and worship. As for Ishmael (peace be upon him), he was patient in submitting to being sacrificed, he was patient in remaining in a land with no crops, no pasture and no building, and he was patient in building the House. So Allah, exalted is He, honoured him without doubt and brought forth from his loins the Seal of the Prophets. As for Idris (peace be upon him), his story has already passed in Surah Maryam (peace be upon her).

Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "He was sent to his people as a caller to Allah, exalted is He, but they refused, so Allah destroyed them and raised Idris to the fourth heaven." As for Dhu al-Kifl, there are several issues concerning him:

The first issue: it contains two discussions.

The first: al-Zajjaj said: al-kifl in the language is the cloth placed on the rump of a camel. Al-kifl also means a share. They differed over why he was named by this name, in several respects:

One of them, which is the saying of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun), is that he had double the works of the prophets (peace be upon them) in his time and double their reward.

The second: Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, in one narration: "A prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel was given by Allah kingship and prophethood. Then Allah revealed to him: 'I intend to take your soul, so present your kingship to the Children of Israel; whoever undertakes for you that he will pray at night until morning, fast by day without breaking his fast, and judge between people without becoming angry, then hand your kingship over to him.' That prophet stood among the Children of Israel and informed them of this. A young man stood up and said: 'I will undertake this for you.' He said to the people: 'Whoever is older than you, sit down.' Then he called out a second and a third time, and the man stood up and said: 'I will undertake these three for you.' So he handed over his kingship to him, and he fulfilled what he had guaranteed. Iblis envied him; so he came to him at the time he wished to take his midday rest and said: 'I have a debtor who has delayed my right, and I have invited him to you, but he refused; so send with me someone who will bring him to you.' He sent someone with him and sat waiting until his midday rest had passed, and he called to his prayer and prayed all night until morning. Then he came to him the next day at midday rest and said: 'The man for whom I asked your permission is at such-and-such a place; do not leave until I bring him to you.' He went off and remained waiting until his midday rest had passed; then he came to him and said: 'He fled from me.' Dhu al-Kifl went on to his prayer and prayed his night until morning. Then Iblis came to him, made himself known to him, and said: 'I envied you because of Allah's protection of you, so I wanted to make you go out so that you would not fulfil what you had undertaken.' Allah, exalted is He, thanked him for that and gave him prophethood, and he was named 'Dhu al-Kifl'." On this view, the meaning of al-kifl here is the guarantee (al-kafala).

The third: Mujahid said: When Elisha (peace be upon him) grew old, he said: "If only I could appoint a man over the people during my lifetime, so that I could see how he acts." He gathered the people and said: "Who will take on [this duty] from me?" until he appointed him for three [days], praying by night, fasting by day, and judging without anger. Ali (may Allah honour his face) mentioned something similar to what Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) mentioned of Iblis's action and his causing him to miss the midday rest for three days, and he added that Dhu al-Kifl said to the doorkeeper on the third day: "Sleep has overcome me, so do not let anyone approach this door until I have slept, for the sleepiness has become hard upon me." Iblis came, but the doorkeeper did not admit him; so he entered the house through a window and climbed in, and there he was knocking on the door from inside. The man woke up and reproached the doorkeeper, who said: "I was not given any order from my side." He got up to the door, and it was locked, and Iblis was in the house in the form of an old man. He said to him: "Do you sleep while the litigants are at the door?" He recognised him and said: "You are Iblis." He said: "Yes; you have defeated me in everything, so I did these deeds to anger you, but Allah protected you from me." He was therefore named Dhu al-Kifl, because he fulfilled what he had undertaken.

The second issue: Abu Musa al-Ashari (may Allah be pleased with him) and Mujahid said: Dhu al-Kifl was not a prophet, but he was a righteous servant. Al-Hasan and most scholars said: he was among the prophets (peace be upon them). This view is preferable for several reasons:

One of them: Dhu al-Kifl may be either a title (laqab) or a proper name, and the nearer possibility is that it is meaningful, since when a name can be understood as conveying a meaning it is preferable to a title. Having established this, we say: al-kifl is the share, and the apparent meaning is that Allah, exalted is He, named him thus as an honour, so that kifl must be the share of reward. He was named thus because his work and the reward of his work were double the work and reward of others. There were prophets in his time, as is narrated, and one who is not a prophet cannot be superior to the prophets.

The second: He, exalted is He, joined his mention with the mention of Ishmael and Idris, and the purpose is to mention the excellent of His servants so that they may be emulated, which indicates his prophethood.

The third: The surah is titled "Surah al-Anbiya" (The Prophets), so everyone Allah, exalted is He, mentions in it is a prophet.

The third issue: It has been said that Dhu al-Kifl was Zechariah; it has been said he was Joshua; and it has been said he was Elijah. Then they said: five of the prophets were named by Allah, exalted is He, with two names: Israel and Jacob; Elijah and Dhu al-Kifl; Jesus and the Messiah; Jonah and Dhu al-Nun; Muhammad and Ahmad.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿each of them was among the patient﴾, that is, in upholding the command of Allah, exalted is He, and in bearing harm in support of His religion. As for His saying: ﴿And We admitted them into Our mercy﴾, Muqatil said: the mercy is prophethood. Others said: rather, it encompasses all acts of righteousness and goodness.
