[The verses mean: "Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has preceded, they will be kept far from it (Hell). They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire. The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: 'This is your day which you were promised.'"]

اعْلَمْ أنَّ مِنَ النّاسِ مَن زَعَمَ أنَّ ابْنَ الزِّبَعْرى لَمّا أوْرَدَ ذَلِكَ السُّؤالَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ بَقِيَ ساكِتًا حَتّى أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ جَوابًا عَنْ سُؤالِهِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ كالِاسْتِثْناءِ مِن تِلْكَ الآيَةِ، وأمّا نَحْنُ فَقَدَ بَيَّنّا فَسادَ هَذا القَوْلِ، وذَكَرْنا أنَّ سُؤالَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ وارِدًا، وأنَّهُ لا حاجَةَ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِهِ إلى نُزُولِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ، وإذا ثَبَتَ هَذا لَمْ يَبْقَ هاهُنا إلّا أحَدُ أمْرَيْنِ:

Know that some people claim that when Ibn al-Zib'ara raised that objection to the Messenger (ﷺ), he remained silent until God Most High revealed this verse as an answer to his question, because this verse is like an exception to that verse. As for us, we have already demonstrated the invalidity of this view, and we mentioned that his question was not a valid one, and that there is no need to revelation of this verse to dispel his question. Once this is established, only one of two possibilities remains:

الأوَّلُ: أنْ يُقالَ: إنَّ عادَةَ اللَّهِ تَعالى أنَّهُ مَتى شَرَحَ عِقابَ الكُفّارِ أرْدَفَهُ بِشَرْحِ ثَوابِ الأبْرارِ، فَلِهَذا السَّبَبِ ذَكَرَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَقِيبَ تِلْكَ فَهي عامَّةٌ في حَقِّ كُلِّ المُؤْمِنِينَ.

The first: it may be said that it is God Most High's custom that whenever He describes the punishment of the disbelievers, He follows it with a description of the reward of the righteous. For this reason He mentioned this verse right after that one, so it is general in its application to all believers.

الثّانِي: أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في تِلْكَ الواقِعَةِ لِتَكُونَ كالتَّأْكِيدِ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِ ابْنِ الزِّبَعْرى، ثُمَّ مَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِعُمُومِ اللَّفْظِ لا بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ، وهو الحَقُّ، أجْراها عَلى عُمُومِها؛ فَتَكُونُ المَلائِكَةُ والمَسِيحُ وعُزَيْرٌ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ داخِلِينَ فِيها، لا أنَّ

The second: this verse was revealed in that incident so as to serve as a confirmation in dismissing Ibn al-Zib'ara's objection. Then, whoever says that the ruling is based on the general wording and not on the specific occasion of revelation (and this is the correct view) applies it in its generality, so that the angels, the Messiah and 'Uzayr (peace be upon them) are included in it, rather than

صفحة ١٩٦
الآيَةَ مُخْتَصَّةٌ بِهِمْ، ومَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ خَصَّصَ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ بِهَؤُلاءِ فَقَطْ.

the verse being specific to them. And whoever says that the ruling is based on the specific occasion of revelation restricts His saying "Indeed, those who" to these alone.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ فَقالَ صاحِبُ ”الكَشّافِ“: الحُسْنى الخَصْلَةُ المُفَضَّلَةُ، والحُسْنى تَأْنِيثُ الأحْسَنِ، وهي إمّا السَّعادَةُ وإمّا البُشْرى بِالثَّوابِ، وإمّا التَّوْفِيقُ لِلطّاعَةِ، والحاصِلُ أنَّ مُثْبِتِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوا الحُسْنى عَلى وعْدِ العَفْوِ، ومُنْكِرِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوهُ عَلى وعْدِ الثَّوابِ، ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى شَرَحَ مِن أحْوالِ ثَوابِهِمْ أُمُورًا خَمْسَةً:

As for His saying: ﴿has preceded for them from Us the best [reward]﴾, the author of al-Kashshaf said: al-husna is the preferred quality; al-husna is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the best), and it may be happiness, or the good tidings of reward, or divine grace to obey. The point is that those who affirm pardon (al-'afw) interpreted al-husna as the promise of pardon, while those who deny pardon interpreted it as the promise of reward. Then He, glorified and exalted, described five matters concerning their reward:

أحَدُها قَوْلُهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ فَقالَ أهْلُ العَفْوِ: مَعْناهُ أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُخْرَجُونَ، واحْتَجُّوا عَلَيْهِ بِوَجْهَيْنِ:

The first is His saying: ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾. The people of pardon said: its meaning is "they will be removed from it," and they argued for this on two grounds:

الأوَّلُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ أثْبَتَ الوُرُودَ وهو الدُّخُولُ، فَدَلَّ عَلى أنَّ هَذا الإبْعادَ هو الإخْراجُ.

The first: His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which affirmed the passing over (wurud), which is entering. This shows that this "keeping far" means removal.

الثّانِي: أنَّ إبْعادَ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ لا يَصِحُّ إلّا إذا كانا مُتَقارِبَيْنِ؛ لِأنَّهُما لَوْ كانا مُتَباعِدَيْنِ اسْتَحالَ إبْعادُ أحَدِهِما عَنِ الآخَرِ؛ لَأنَّ تَحْصِيلَ الحاصِلِ مُحالٌ.

The second: keeping one thing far from another is valid only if the two are close to each other; for if they were far apart, it would be impossible to keep one away from the other, because making what is already attained attained again is impossible.

واحْتَجَّ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ بِأُمُورٍ:

Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar argued against this first view on several grounds:

أحَدُها: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ في الدُّنْيا ولَيْسَ هَذا حالُ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ لَوْ صَحَّ ذَلِكَ.

The first: His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ implies that the promise of their reward was given in this world beforehand, and this is not the condition of one who is brought out of the Fire, even if that were valid.

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ وكَيْفَ يَدْخُلُ في ذَلِكَ مَن وقَعَ فِيها.

The second: He said ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾, and how can one who has fallen into it be included in this?

وثالِثُها: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ يَمْنَعُ مِن ذَلِكَ.

The third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ and His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ prevent this.

والجَوابُ عَنِ الأوَّلِ: لا نُسَلِّمُ أنْ [ يُقالَ ] المُرادُ مِن قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ هو أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ، ولِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالعَفْوِ ؟ سَلَّمْنا أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالثَّوابِ، لَكِنْ لِمَ قُلْتُمْ: إنَّ الوَعْدَ بِالثَّوابِ لا يَلِيقُ بِحالِ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ، فَإنَّ عِنْدَنا المُحابَطَةَ باطِلَةٌ، ويَجُوزُ الجَمْعُ بَيْنَ اسْتِحْقاقِ الثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، وعَنِ الثّانِي: أنّا بَيَّنّا أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ لا يُمْكِنُ إجْراؤُهُ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ إلّا في حَقِّ مَن كانَ في النّارِ، وعَنِ الثّالِثِ: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ مَخْصُوصٌ بِما بَعْدَ الخُرُوجِ.

As for the answer to the first: we do not accept that it means the promise of their reward had already been given. Why could it not be that the "best" means the prior promise of pardon? Even if we grant that it means the prior promise of reward, why do you say that a promise of reward is not fitting for the condition of one who comes out of the Fire? For in our view, *muhabata* (the nullification of good deeds by sins) is false, and it is permissible to combine deserving reward and punishment. As for the answer to the second: we have shown that His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ cannot be applied to its apparent meaning except regarding one who was in the Fire. As for the answer to the third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ is restricted to what comes after the exit.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ فالفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ هو عَذابُ الكُفّارِ، وهَذا بِطَرِيقِ المَفْهُومِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّهم يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأصْغَرُ، فَإنْ لَمْ يَدُلَّ عَلَيْهِ فَلا أقَلَّ مِن أنْ لا يَدُلَّ عَلى ثُبُوتِهِ ولا عَلى عَدَمِهِ.

As for His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾: the greatest terror is the punishment of the disbelievers. By way of implication (mafhum), this indicates that they may be grieved by the lesser terror; and if it does not indicate this, then at least it does not indicate either its affirmation or its negation.

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي: في تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ أنَّ المُرادَ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى لا يَدْخُلُونَ النّارَ ولا يَقْرَبُونَها البَتَّةَ، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ بَطَلَ قَوْلُ مَن يَقُولُ: إنَّ جَمِيعَ النّاسِ يَرِدُونَ النّارَ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُونَ إلى الجَنَّةِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ مانِعَةٌ مِنهُ، وحِينَئِذٍ يَجِبُ التَّوْفِيقُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ.

The second view regarding His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ is that it means those for whom the best has preceded from Us will not enter the Fire and will never draw near to it at all. On this view, the claim of those who say that all people will pass over the Fire and then go out to Paradise is refuted, because this verse prevents it; and then it becomes necessary to reconcile it with His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which has already been discussed.

الصِّفَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ والحَسِيسُ الصَّوْتُ الَّذِي يُحَسُّ، وفِيهِ سُؤالانِ:

The second description: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾. The *hasis* is the sound that is perceived. On this there are two questions:

الأوَّلُ: أيُّ وجْهٍ في أنْ لا يَسْمَعُوا حَسِيسَها مِنَ البِشارَةِ، ولَوْ سَمِعُوهُ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ حالُهم ؟

The first: what is the point of their not hearing its sound as a good tiding, since even if they heard it, their condition would not change?

قُلْنا: المُرادُ تَأْكِيدُ بُعْدِهِمْ عَنْها؛ لِأنَّ مَن لَمْ يَدْخُلْها وقَرُبَ مِنها قَدْ يَسْمَعُ حَسِيسَها.

We say: the purpose is to emphasize their distance from it, because one who has not entered it but is near to it may hear its sound.

السُّؤالُ الثّانِي: ألَيْسَ أنَّ أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ يَرَوْنَ أهْلَ النّارِ، فَكَيْفَ لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَ النّارِ ؟

The second question: do not the people of Paradise see the people of the Fire? So how can they not hear the sound of the Fire?

الجَوابُ: إذا حَمَلْناهُ عَلى التَّأْكِيدِ زالَ هَذا السُّؤالُ.

The answer: if we take it as emphasis, this question disappears.

الصِّفَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ والشَّهْوَةُ طَلَبُ النَّفْسِ لِلَذَّةٍ، يَعْنِي: نَعِيمُها مُؤَبَّدٌ، قالَ العارِفُونَ: لِلنُّفُوسِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْقُلُوبِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْأرْواحِ شَهْوَةٌ، وقالَ الجُنَيْدُ: سَبَقَتِ العِنايَةُ في البِدايَةِ، فَظَهَرَتِ الوِلايَةُ في النِّهايَةِ.

The third description: His saying ﴿and they will abide forever in what their souls desire﴾. *Shahwa* (desire) is the soul's seeking of pleasure; that is, its bliss is everlasting. The gnostics (al-'arifun) said: the souls have a desire, the hearts have a desire, and the spirits have a desire. Al-Junayd said: "Divine care preceded at the beginning, so guardianship (wilaya) appeared at the end."

الصِّفَةُ الرّابِعَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ وفِيهِ وُجُوهٌ:

The fourth description: His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾. On this there are several views:

أحَدُها: أنَّها النَّفْخَةُ الأخِيرَةُ لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾ [النمل: ٨٧] .

The first: it is the final blast, based on His saying: ﴿And the day the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck with terror﴾ [al-Naml 27:87].

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ المَوْتُ، قالُوا: إذا اسْتَقَرَّ أهْلُ الجَنَّةِ في الجَنَّةِ وأهْلُ النّارِ في النّارِ، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ تَعالى جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ومَعَهُ المَوْتُ في صُورَةِ كَبْشٍ أمْلَحَ فَيَقُولُ: لِأهْلِ الدّارَيْنِ أتَعْرِفُونَ هَذا ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: لا، فَيَقُولُ: هَذا المَوْتُ، ثُمَّ يَذْبَحُهُ؛ ثُمَّ يُنادِي يا أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ، خُلُودٌ ولا مَوْتَ أبَدًا، وكَذَلِكَ لِأهْلِ النّارِ،

The second: it is death. They said: when the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, God Most High sends Gabriel (peace be upon him), and with him Death in the form of a white-speckled ram. He says to the people of both abodes: "Do you recognize this?" They say: "No." He says: "This is Death." Then he slaughters it, and then calls out: "O people of Paradise, eternal abiding with no death ever," and likewise for the people of the Fire.

صفحة ١٩٧
واحْتَجَّ هَذا القائِلُ بِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ إنَّما ذُكِرَ بَعْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وهم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾ فَلا بُدَّ وأنْ يَكُونَ لِأحَدِهِما تَعَلُّقٌ بِالآخَرِ، والفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ الَّذِي هو يُنافِي الخُلُودَ هو المَوْتُ.

This speaker argued that His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ was mentioned after His saying ﴿and they abide therein forever﴾; so one of them must be connected to the other, and the greatest terror which contradicts eternal abiding is death.

وثالِثُها: قالَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ: هو إطْباقُ النّارِ عَلى أهْلِها فَيَفْزَعُونَ لِذَلِكَ فَزْعَةً عَظِيمَةً، قالَ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ: الأوْلى في ذَلِكَ أنَّهُ الفَزَعُ مِنَ النّارِ عِنْدَ مُشاهَدَتِها؛ لِأنَّهُ لا فَزَعَ أكْبَرُ مِن ذَلِكَ، فَإذا بَيَّنَ تَعالى أنَّ ذَلِكَ لا يَحْزُنُهم فَقَدْ صَحَّ أنَّ المُؤْمِنَ آمِنٌ مِن أهْوالِ يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ، وهَذا ضَعِيفٌ؛ لِأنَّ عَذابَ النّارِ عَلى مَراتِبَ فَعَذابُ الكُفّارِ أشَدُّ مِن عَذابِ الفُسّاقِ، وإذا كانَتْ مَراتِبُ التَّعْذِيبِ بِالنّارِ مُتَفاوِتَةً كانَتْ مَراتِبُ الفَزَعِ مِنها مُتَفاوِتَةً، فَلا يَلْزَمُ مِن نَفْيِ الفَزَعِ الأكْبَرِ نَفْيُ الفَزَعِ مِنَ النّارِ.

The third: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the closing of the Fire over its people, so they are struck with a great terror at that. Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar said: the more likely view is that it is the terror of the Fire at the moment of witnessing it, since there is no greater terror than that. So when God Most High declares that this will not grieve them, it is established that the believer is safe from the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. But this is weak, because the punishment of the Fire has degrees: the punishment of the disbelievers is more severe than that of the sinners, and if the degrees of punishment by the Fire vary, the degrees of terror from it also vary. Thus, negating the greatest terror does not necessarily negate terror of the Fire.

الصِّفَةُ الخامِسَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ: هُمُ الحَفَظَةُ الَّذِينَ كَتَبُوا أعْمالَهم وأقْوالَهم، ويَقُولُونَ لَهم مُبَشِّرِينَ: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ .

The fifth description: His saying ﴿and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your day which you were promised"﴾. Al-Dahhak said: they are the guardian angels who recorded their deeds and words, and they say to them, giving good tidings: ﴿This is your day which you were promised.﴾

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾

[The verses mean: "Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has preceded, they will be kept far from it (Hell). They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire. The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: 'This is your day which you were promised.'"]

اعْلَمْ أنَّ مِنَ النّاسِ مَن زَعَمَ أنَّ ابْنَ الزِّبَعْرى لَمّا أوْرَدَ ذَلِكَ السُّؤالَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ بَقِيَ ساكِتًا حَتّى أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ جَوابًا عَنْ سُؤالِهِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ كالِاسْتِثْناءِ مِن تِلْكَ الآيَةِ، وأمّا نَحْنُ فَقَدَ بَيَّنّا فَسادَ هَذا القَوْلِ، وذَكَرْنا أنَّ سُؤالَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ وارِدًا، وأنَّهُ لا حاجَةَ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِهِ إلى نُزُولِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ، وإذا ثَبَتَ هَذا لَمْ يَبْقَ هاهُنا إلّا أحَدُ أمْرَيْنِ:

Know that some people claim that when Ibn al-Zib'ara raised that objection to the Messenger (ﷺ), he remained silent until God Most High revealed this verse as an answer to his question, because this verse is like an exception to that verse. As for us, we have already demonstrated the invalidity of this view, and we mentioned that his question was not a valid one, and that there is no need to revelation of this verse to dispel his question. Once this is established, only one of two possibilities remains:

الأوَّلُ: أنْ يُقالَ: إنَّ عادَةَ اللَّهِ تَعالى أنَّهُ مَتى شَرَحَ عِقابَ الكُفّارِ أرْدَفَهُ بِشَرْحِ ثَوابِ الأبْرارِ، فَلِهَذا السَّبَبِ ذَكَرَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَقِيبَ تِلْكَ فَهي عامَّةٌ في حَقِّ كُلِّ المُؤْمِنِينَ.

The first: it may be said that it is God Most High's custom that whenever He describes the punishment of the disbelievers, He follows it with a description of the reward of the righteous. For this reason He mentioned this verse right after that one, so it is general in its application to all believers.

الثّانِي: أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في تِلْكَ الواقِعَةِ لِتَكُونَ كالتَّأْكِيدِ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِ ابْنِ الزِّبَعْرى، ثُمَّ مَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِعُمُومِ اللَّفْظِ لا بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ، وهو الحَقُّ، أجْراها عَلى عُمُومِها؛ فَتَكُونُ المَلائِكَةُ والمَسِيحُ وعُزَيْرٌ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ داخِلِينَ فِيها، لا أنَّ

The second: this verse was revealed in that incident so as to serve as a confirmation in dismissing Ibn al-Zib'ara's objection. Then, whoever says that the ruling is based on the general wording and not on the specific occasion of revelation (and this is the correct view) applies it in its generality, so that the angels, the Messiah and 'Uzayr (peace be upon them) are included in it, rather than

صفحة ١٩٦
الآيَةَ مُخْتَصَّةٌ بِهِمْ، ومَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ خَصَّصَ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ بِهَؤُلاءِ فَقَطْ.

the verse being specific to them. And whoever says that the ruling is based on the specific occasion of revelation restricts His saying "Indeed, those who" to these alone.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ فَقالَ صاحِبُ ”الكَشّافِ“: الحُسْنى الخَصْلَةُ المُفَضَّلَةُ، والحُسْنى تَأْنِيثُ الأحْسَنِ، وهي إمّا السَّعادَةُ وإمّا البُشْرى بِالثَّوابِ، وإمّا التَّوْفِيقُ لِلطّاعَةِ، والحاصِلُ أنَّ مُثْبِتِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوا الحُسْنى عَلى وعْدِ العَفْوِ، ومُنْكِرِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوهُ عَلى وعْدِ الثَّوابِ، ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى شَرَحَ مِن أحْوالِ ثَوابِهِمْ أُمُورًا خَمْسَةً:

As for His saying: ﴿has preceded for them from Us the best [reward]﴾, the author of al-Kashshaf said: al-husna is the preferred quality; al-husna is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the best), and it may be happiness, or the good tidings of reward, or divine grace to obey. The point is that those who affirm pardon (al-'afw) interpreted al-husna as the promise of pardon, while those who deny pardon interpreted it as the promise of reward. Then He, glorified and exalted, described five matters concerning their reward:

أحَدُها قَوْلُهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ فَقالَ أهْلُ العَفْوِ: مَعْناهُ أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُخْرَجُونَ، واحْتَجُّوا عَلَيْهِ بِوَجْهَيْنِ:

The first is His saying: ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾. The people of pardon said: its meaning is "they will be removed from it," and they argued for this on two grounds:

الأوَّلُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ أثْبَتَ الوُرُودَ وهو الدُّخُولُ، فَدَلَّ عَلى أنَّ هَذا الإبْعادَ هو الإخْراجُ.

The first: His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which affirmed the passing over (wurud), which is entering. This shows that this "keeping far" means removal.

الثّانِي: أنَّ إبْعادَ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ لا يَصِحُّ إلّا إذا كانا مُتَقارِبَيْنِ؛ لِأنَّهُما لَوْ كانا مُتَباعِدَيْنِ اسْتَحالَ إبْعادُ أحَدِهِما عَنِ الآخَرِ؛ لَأنَّ تَحْصِيلَ الحاصِلِ مُحالٌ.

The second: keeping one thing far from another is valid only if the two are close to each other; for if they were far apart, it would be impossible to keep one away from the other, because making what is already attained attained again is impossible.

واحْتَجَّ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ بِأُمُورٍ:

Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar argued against this first view on several grounds:

أحَدُها: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ في الدُّنْيا ولَيْسَ هَذا حالُ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ لَوْ صَحَّ ذَلِكَ.

The first: His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ implies that the promise of their reward was given in this world beforehand, and this is not the condition of one who is brought out of the Fire, even if that were valid.

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ وكَيْفَ يَدْخُلُ في ذَلِكَ مَن وقَعَ فِيها.

The second: He said ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾, and how can one who has fallen into it be included in this?

وثالِثُها: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ يَمْنَعُ مِن ذَلِكَ.

The third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ and His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ prevent this.

والجَوابُ عَنِ الأوَّلِ: لا نُسَلِّمُ أنْ [ يُقالَ ] المُرادُ مِن قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ هو أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ، ولِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالعَفْوِ ؟ سَلَّمْنا أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالثَّوابِ، لَكِنْ لِمَ قُلْتُمْ: إنَّ الوَعْدَ بِالثَّوابِ لا يَلِيقُ بِحالِ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ، فَإنَّ عِنْدَنا المُحابَطَةَ باطِلَةٌ، ويَجُوزُ الجَمْعُ بَيْنَ اسْتِحْقاقِ الثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، وعَنِ الثّانِي: أنّا بَيَّنّا أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ لا يُمْكِنُ إجْراؤُهُ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ إلّا في حَقِّ مَن كانَ في النّارِ، وعَنِ الثّالِثِ: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ مَخْصُوصٌ بِما بَعْدَ الخُرُوجِ.

As for the answer to the first: we do not accept that it means the promise of their reward had already been given. Why could it not be that the "best" means the prior promise of pardon? Even if we grant that it means the prior promise of reward, why do you say that a promise of reward is not fitting for the condition of one who comes out of the Fire? For in our view, *muhabata* (the nullification of good deeds by sins) is false, and it is permissible to combine deserving reward and punishment. As for the answer to the second: we have shown that His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ cannot be applied to its apparent meaning except regarding one who was in the Fire. As for the answer to the third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ is restricted to what comes after the exit.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ فالفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ هو عَذابُ الكُفّارِ، وهَذا بِطَرِيقِ المَفْهُومِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّهم يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأصْغَرُ، فَإنْ لَمْ يَدُلَّ عَلَيْهِ فَلا أقَلَّ مِن أنْ لا يَدُلَّ عَلى ثُبُوتِهِ ولا عَلى عَدَمِهِ.

As for His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾: the greatest terror is the punishment of the disbelievers. By way of implication (mafhum), this indicates that they may be grieved by the lesser terror; and if it does not indicate this, then at least it does not indicate either its affirmation or its negation.

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي: في تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ أنَّ المُرادَ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى لا يَدْخُلُونَ النّارَ ولا يَقْرَبُونَها البَتَّةَ، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ بَطَلَ قَوْلُ مَن يَقُولُ: إنَّ جَمِيعَ النّاسِ يَرِدُونَ النّارَ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُونَ إلى الجَنَّةِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ مانِعَةٌ مِنهُ، وحِينَئِذٍ يَجِبُ التَّوْفِيقُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ.

The second view regarding His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ is that it means those for whom the best has preceded from Us will not enter the Fire and will never draw near to it at all. On this view, the claim of those who say that all people will pass over the Fire and then go out to Paradise is refuted, because this verse prevents it; and then it becomes necessary to reconcile it with His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which has already been discussed.

الصِّفَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ والحَسِيسُ الصَّوْتُ الَّذِي يُحَسُّ، وفِيهِ سُؤالانِ:

The second description: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾. The *hasis* is the sound that is perceived. On this there are two questions:

الأوَّلُ: أيُّ وجْهٍ في أنْ لا يَسْمَعُوا حَسِيسَها مِنَ البِشارَةِ، ولَوْ سَمِعُوهُ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ حالُهم ؟

The first: what is the point of their not hearing its sound as a good tiding, since even if they heard it, their condition would not change?

قُلْنا: المُرادُ تَأْكِيدُ بُعْدِهِمْ عَنْها؛ لِأنَّ مَن لَمْ يَدْخُلْها وقَرُبَ مِنها قَدْ يَسْمَعُ حَسِيسَها.

We say: the purpose is to emphasize their distance from it, because one who has not entered it but is near to it may hear its sound.

السُّؤالُ الثّانِي: ألَيْسَ أنَّ أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ يَرَوْنَ أهْلَ النّارِ، فَكَيْفَ لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَ النّارِ ؟

The second question: do not the people of Paradise see the people of the Fire? So how can they not hear the sound of the Fire?

الجَوابُ: إذا حَمَلْناهُ عَلى التَّأْكِيدِ زالَ هَذا السُّؤالُ.

The answer: if we take it as emphasis, this question disappears.

الصِّفَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ والشَّهْوَةُ طَلَبُ النَّفْسِ لِلَذَّةٍ، يَعْنِي: نَعِيمُها مُؤَبَّدٌ، قالَ العارِفُونَ: لِلنُّفُوسِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْقُلُوبِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْأرْواحِ شَهْوَةٌ، وقالَ الجُنَيْدُ: سَبَقَتِ العِنايَةُ في البِدايَةِ، فَظَهَرَتِ الوِلايَةُ في النِّهايَةِ.

The third description: His saying ﴿and they will abide forever in what their souls desire﴾. *Shahwa* (desire) is the soul's seeking of pleasure; that is, its bliss is everlasting. The gnostics (al-'arifun) said: the souls have a desire, the hearts have a desire, and the spirits have a desire. Al-Junayd said: "Divine care preceded at the beginning, so guardianship (wilaya) appeared at the end."

الصِّفَةُ الرّابِعَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ وفِيهِ وُجُوهٌ:

The fourth description: His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾. On this there are several views:

أحَدُها: أنَّها النَّفْخَةُ الأخِيرَةُ لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾ [النمل: ٨٧] .

The first: it is the final blast, based on His saying: ﴿And the day the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck with terror﴾ [al-Naml 27:87].

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ المَوْتُ، قالُوا: إذا اسْتَقَرَّ أهْلُ الجَنَّةِ في الجَنَّةِ وأهْلُ النّارِ في النّارِ، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ تَعالى جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ومَعَهُ المَوْتُ في صُورَةِ كَبْشٍ أمْلَحَ فَيَقُولُ: لِأهْلِ الدّارَيْنِ أتَعْرِفُونَ هَذا ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: لا، فَيَقُولُ: هَذا المَوْتُ، ثُمَّ يَذْبَحُهُ؛ ثُمَّ يُنادِي يا أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ، خُلُودٌ ولا مَوْتَ أبَدًا، وكَذَلِكَ لِأهْلِ النّارِ،

The second: it is death. They said: when the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, God Most High sends Gabriel (peace be upon him), and with him Death in the form of a white-speckled ram. He says to the people of both abodes: "Do you recognize this?" They say: "No." He says: "This is Death." Then he slaughters it, and then calls out: "O people of Paradise, eternal abiding with no death ever," and likewise for the people of the Fire.

صفحة ١٩٧
واحْتَجَّ هَذا القائِلُ بِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ إنَّما ذُكِرَ بَعْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وهم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾ فَلا بُدَّ وأنْ يَكُونَ لِأحَدِهِما تَعَلُّقٌ بِالآخَرِ، والفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ الَّذِي هو يُنافِي الخُلُودَ هو المَوْتُ.

This speaker argued that His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ was mentioned after His saying ﴿and they abide therein forever﴾; so one of them must be connected to the other, and the greatest terror which contradicts eternal abiding is death.

وثالِثُها: قالَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ: هو إطْباقُ النّارِ عَلى أهْلِها فَيَفْزَعُونَ لِذَلِكَ فَزْعَةً عَظِيمَةً، قالَ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ: الأوْلى في ذَلِكَ أنَّهُ الفَزَعُ مِنَ النّارِ عِنْدَ مُشاهَدَتِها؛ لِأنَّهُ لا فَزَعَ أكْبَرُ مِن ذَلِكَ، فَإذا بَيَّنَ تَعالى أنَّ ذَلِكَ لا يَحْزُنُهم فَقَدْ صَحَّ أنَّ المُؤْمِنَ آمِنٌ مِن أهْوالِ يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ، وهَذا ضَعِيفٌ؛ لِأنَّ عَذابَ النّارِ عَلى مَراتِبَ فَعَذابُ الكُفّارِ أشَدُّ مِن عَذابِ الفُسّاقِ، وإذا كانَتْ مَراتِبُ التَّعْذِيبِ بِالنّارِ مُتَفاوِتَةً كانَتْ مَراتِبُ الفَزَعِ مِنها مُتَفاوِتَةً، فَلا يَلْزَمُ مِن نَفْيِ الفَزَعِ الأكْبَرِ نَفْيُ الفَزَعِ مِنَ النّارِ.

The third: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the closing of the Fire over its people, so they are struck with a great terror at that. Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar said: the more likely view is that it is the terror of the Fire at the moment of witnessing it, since there is no greater terror than that. So when God Most High declares that this will not grieve them, it is established that the believer is safe from the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. But this is weak, because the punishment of the Fire has degrees: the punishment of the disbelievers is more severe than that of the sinners, and if the degrees of punishment by the Fire vary, the degrees of terror from it also vary. Thus, negating the greatest terror does not necessarily negate terror of the Fire.

الصِّفَةُ الخامِسَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ: هُمُ الحَفَظَةُ الَّذِينَ كَتَبُوا أعْمالَهم وأقْوالَهم، ويَقُولُونَ لَهم مُبَشِّرِينَ: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ .

The fifth description: His saying ﴿and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your day which you were promised"﴾. Al-Dahhak said: they are the guardian angels who recorded their deeds and words, and they say to them, giving good tidings: ﴿This is your day which you were promised.﴾

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾

[The verses mean: "Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has preceded, they will be kept far from it (Hell). They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire. The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: 'This is your day which you were promised.'"]

اعْلَمْ أنَّ مِنَ النّاسِ مَن زَعَمَ أنَّ ابْنَ الزِّبَعْرى لَمّا أوْرَدَ ذَلِكَ السُّؤالَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ بَقِيَ ساكِتًا حَتّى أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ جَوابًا عَنْ سُؤالِهِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ كالِاسْتِثْناءِ مِن تِلْكَ الآيَةِ، وأمّا نَحْنُ فَقَدَ بَيَّنّا فَسادَ هَذا القَوْلِ، وذَكَرْنا أنَّ سُؤالَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ وارِدًا، وأنَّهُ لا حاجَةَ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِهِ إلى نُزُولِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ، وإذا ثَبَتَ هَذا لَمْ يَبْقَ هاهُنا إلّا أحَدُ أمْرَيْنِ:

Know that some people claim that when Ibn al-Zib'ara raised that objection to the Messenger (ﷺ), he remained silent until God Most High revealed this verse as an answer to his question, because this verse is like an exception to that verse. As for us, we have already demonstrated the invalidity of this view, and we mentioned that his question was not a valid one, and that there is no need to revelation of this verse to dispel his question. Once this is established, only one of two possibilities remains:

الأوَّلُ: أنْ يُقالَ: إنَّ عادَةَ اللَّهِ تَعالى أنَّهُ مَتى شَرَحَ عِقابَ الكُفّارِ أرْدَفَهُ بِشَرْحِ ثَوابِ الأبْرارِ، فَلِهَذا السَّبَبِ ذَكَرَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَقِيبَ تِلْكَ فَهي عامَّةٌ في حَقِّ كُلِّ المُؤْمِنِينَ.

The first: it may be said that it is God Most High's custom that whenever He describes the punishment of the disbelievers, He follows it with a description of the reward of the righteous. For this reason He mentioned this verse right after that one, so it is general in its application to all believers.

الثّانِي: أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في تِلْكَ الواقِعَةِ لِتَكُونَ كالتَّأْكِيدِ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِ ابْنِ الزِّبَعْرى، ثُمَّ مَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِعُمُومِ اللَّفْظِ لا بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ، وهو الحَقُّ، أجْراها عَلى عُمُومِها؛ فَتَكُونُ المَلائِكَةُ والمَسِيحُ وعُزَيْرٌ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ داخِلِينَ فِيها، لا أنَّ

The second: this verse was revealed in that incident so as to serve as a confirmation in dismissing Ibn al-Zib'ara's objection. Then, whoever says that the ruling is based on the general wording and not on the specific occasion of revelation (and this is the correct view) applies it in its generality, so that the angels, the Messiah and 'Uzayr (peace be upon them) are included in it, rather than

صفحة ١٩٦
الآيَةَ مُخْتَصَّةٌ بِهِمْ، ومَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ خَصَّصَ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ بِهَؤُلاءِ فَقَطْ.

the verse being specific to them. And whoever says that the ruling is based on the specific occasion of revelation restricts His saying "Indeed, those who" to these alone.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ فَقالَ صاحِبُ ”الكَشّافِ“: الحُسْنى الخَصْلَةُ المُفَضَّلَةُ، والحُسْنى تَأْنِيثُ الأحْسَنِ، وهي إمّا السَّعادَةُ وإمّا البُشْرى بِالثَّوابِ، وإمّا التَّوْفِيقُ لِلطّاعَةِ، والحاصِلُ أنَّ مُثْبِتِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوا الحُسْنى عَلى وعْدِ العَفْوِ، ومُنْكِرِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوهُ عَلى وعْدِ الثَّوابِ، ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى شَرَحَ مِن أحْوالِ ثَوابِهِمْ أُمُورًا خَمْسَةً:

As for His saying: ﴿has preceded for them from Us the best [reward]﴾, the author of al-Kashshaf said: al-husna is the preferred quality; al-husna is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the best), and it may be happiness, or the good tidings of reward, or divine grace to obey. The point is that those who affirm pardon (al-'afw) interpreted al-husna as the promise of pardon, while those who deny pardon interpreted it as the promise of reward. Then He, glorified and exalted, described five matters concerning their reward:

أحَدُها قَوْلُهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ فَقالَ أهْلُ العَفْوِ: مَعْناهُ أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُخْرَجُونَ، واحْتَجُّوا عَلَيْهِ بِوَجْهَيْنِ:

The first is His saying: ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾. The people of pardon said: its meaning is "they will be removed from it," and they argued for this on two grounds:

الأوَّلُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ أثْبَتَ الوُرُودَ وهو الدُّخُولُ، فَدَلَّ عَلى أنَّ هَذا الإبْعادَ هو الإخْراجُ.

The first: His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which affirmed the passing over (wurud), which is entering. This shows that this "keeping far" means removal.

الثّانِي: أنَّ إبْعادَ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ لا يَصِحُّ إلّا إذا كانا مُتَقارِبَيْنِ؛ لِأنَّهُما لَوْ كانا مُتَباعِدَيْنِ اسْتَحالَ إبْعادُ أحَدِهِما عَنِ الآخَرِ؛ لَأنَّ تَحْصِيلَ الحاصِلِ مُحالٌ.

The second: keeping one thing far from another is valid only if the two are close to each other; for if they were far apart, it would be impossible to keep one away from the other, because making what is already attained attained again is impossible.

واحْتَجَّ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ بِأُمُورٍ:

Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar argued against this first view on several grounds:

أحَدُها: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ في الدُّنْيا ولَيْسَ هَذا حالُ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ لَوْ صَحَّ ذَلِكَ.

The first: His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ implies that the promise of their reward was given in this world beforehand, and this is not the condition of one who is brought out of the Fire, even if that were valid.

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ وكَيْفَ يَدْخُلُ في ذَلِكَ مَن وقَعَ فِيها.

The second: He said ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾, and how can one who has fallen into it be included in this?

وثالِثُها: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ يَمْنَعُ مِن ذَلِكَ.

The third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ and His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ prevent this.

والجَوابُ عَنِ الأوَّلِ: لا نُسَلِّمُ أنْ [ يُقالَ ] المُرادُ مِن قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ هو أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ، ولِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالعَفْوِ ؟ سَلَّمْنا أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالثَّوابِ، لَكِنْ لِمَ قُلْتُمْ: إنَّ الوَعْدَ بِالثَّوابِ لا يَلِيقُ بِحالِ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ، فَإنَّ عِنْدَنا المُحابَطَةَ باطِلَةٌ، ويَجُوزُ الجَمْعُ بَيْنَ اسْتِحْقاقِ الثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، وعَنِ الثّانِي: أنّا بَيَّنّا أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ لا يُمْكِنُ إجْراؤُهُ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ إلّا في حَقِّ مَن كانَ في النّارِ، وعَنِ الثّالِثِ: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ مَخْصُوصٌ بِما بَعْدَ الخُرُوجِ.

As for the answer to the first: we do not accept that it means the promise of their reward had already been given. Why could it not be that the "best" means the prior promise of pardon? Even if we grant that it means the prior promise of reward, why do you say that a promise of reward is not fitting for the condition of one who comes out of the Fire? For in our view, *muhabata* (the nullification of good deeds by sins) is false, and it is permissible to combine deserving reward and punishment. As for the answer to the second: we have shown that His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ cannot be applied to its apparent meaning except regarding one who was in the Fire. As for the answer to the third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ is restricted to what comes after the exit.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ فالفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ هو عَذابُ الكُفّارِ، وهَذا بِطَرِيقِ المَفْهُومِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّهم يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأصْغَرُ، فَإنْ لَمْ يَدُلَّ عَلَيْهِ فَلا أقَلَّ مِن أنْ لا يَدُلَّ عَلى ثُبُوتِهِ ولا عَلى عَدَمِهِ.

As for His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾: the greatest terror is the punishment of the disbelievers. By way of implication (mafhum), this indicates that they may be grieved by the lesser terror; and if it does not indicate this, then at least it does not indicate either its affirmation or its negation.

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي: في تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ أنَّ المُرادَ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى لا يَدْخُلُونَ النّارَ ولا يَقْرَبُونَها البَتَّةَ، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ بَطَلَ قَوْلُ مَن يَقُولُ: إنَّ جَمِيعَ النّاسِ يَرِدُونَ النّارَ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُونَ إلى الجَنَّةِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ مانِعَةٌ مِنهُ، وحِينَئِذٍ يَجِبُ التَّوْفِيقُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ.

The second view regarding His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ is that it means those for whom the best has preceded from Us will not enter the Fire and will never draw near to it at all. On this view, the claim of those who say that all people will pass over the Fire and then go out to Paradise is refuted, because this verse prevents it; and then it becomes necessary to reconcile it with His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which has already been discussed.

الصِّفَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ والحَسِيسُ الصَّوْتُ الَّذِي يُحَسُّ، وفِيهِ سُؤالانِ:

The second description: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾. The *hasis* is the sound that is perceived. On this there are two questions:

الأوَّلُ: أيُّ وجْهٍ في أنْ لا يَسْمَعُوا حَسِيسَها مِنَ البِشارَةِ، ولَوْ سَمِعُوهُ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ حالُهم ؟

The first: what is the point of their not hearing its sound as a good tiding, since even if they heard it, their condition would not change?

قُلْنا: المُرادُ تَأْكِيدُ بُعْدِهِمْ عَنْها؛ لِأنَّ مَن لَمْ يَدْخُلْها وقَرُبَ مِنها قَدْ يَسْمَعُ حَسِيسَها.

We say: the purpose is to emphasize their distance from it, because one who has not entered it but is near to it may hear its sound.

السُّؤالُ الثّانِي: ألَيْسَ أنَّ أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ يَرَوْنَ أهْلَ النّارِ، فَكَيْفَ لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَ النّارِ ؟

The second question: do not the people of Paradise see the people of the Fire? So how can they not hear the sound of the Fire?

الجَوابُ: إذا حَمَلْناهُ عَلى التَّأْكِيدِ زالَ هَذا السُّؤالُ.

The answer: if we take it as emphasis, this question disappears.

الصِّفَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ والشَّهْوَةُ طَلَبُ النَّفْسِ لِلَذَّةٍ، يَعْنِي: نَعِيمُها مُؤَبَّدٌ، قالَ العارِفُونَ: لِلنُّفُوسِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْقُلُوبِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْأرْواحِ شَهْوَةٌ، وقالَ الجُنَيْدُ: سَبَقَتِ العِنايَةُ في البِدايَةِ، فَظَهَرَتِ الوِلايَةُ في النِّهايَةِ.

The third description: His saying ﴿and they will abide forever in what their souls desire﴾. *Shahwa* (desire) is the soul's seeking of pleasure; that is, its bliss is everlasting. The gnostics (al-'arifun) said: the souls have a desire, the hearts have a desire, and the spirits have a desire. Al-Junayd said: "Divine care preceded at the beginning, so guardianship (wilaya) appeared at the end."

الصِّفَةُ الرّابِعَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ وفِيهِ وُجُوهٌ:

The fourth description: His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾. On this there are several views:

أحَدُها: أنَّها النَّفْخَةُ الأخِيرَةُ لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾ [النمل: ٨٧] .

The first: it is the final blast, based on His saying: ﴿And the day the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck with terror﴾ [al-Naml 27:87].

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ المَوْتُ، قالُوا: إذا اسْتَقَرَّ أهْلُ الجَنَّةِ في الجَنَّةِ وأهْلُ النّارِ في النّارِ، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ تَعالى جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ومَعَهُ المَوْتُ في صُورَةِ كَبْشٍ أمْلَحَ فَيَقُولُ: لِأهْلِ الدّارَيْنِ أتَعْرِفُونَ هَذا ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: لا، فَيَقُولُ: هَذا المَوْتُ، ثُمَّ يَذْبَحُهُ؛ ثُمَّ يُنادِي يا أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ، خُلُودٌ ولا مَوْتَ أبَدًا، وكَذَلِكَ لِأهْلِ النّارِ،

The second: it is death. They said: when the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, God Most High sends Gabriel (peace be upon him), and with him Death in the form of a white-speckled ram. He says to the people of both abodes: "Do you recognize this?" They say: "No." He says: "This is Death." Then he slaughters it, and then calls out: "O people of Paradise, eternal abiding with no death ever," and likewise for the people of the Fire.

صفحة ١٩٧
واحْتَجَّ هَذا القائِلُ بِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ إنَّما ذُكِرَ بَعْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وهم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾ فَلا بُدَّ وأنْ يَكُونَ لِأحَدِهِما تَعَلُّقٌ بِالآخَرِ، والفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ الَّذِي هو يُنافِي الخُلُودَ هو المَوْتُ.

This speaker argued that His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ was mentioned after His saying ﴿and they abide therein forever﴾; so one of them must be connected to the other, and the greatest terror which contradicts eternal abiding is death.

وثالِثُها: قالَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ: هو إطْباقُ النّارِ عَلى أهْلِها فَيَفْزَعُونَ لِذَلِكَ فَزْعَةً عَظِيمَةً، قالَ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ: الأوْلى في ذَلِكَ أنَّهُ الفَزَعُ مِنَ النّارِ عِنْدَ مُشاهَدَتِها؛ لِأنَّهُ لا فَزَعَ أكْبَرُ مِن ذَلِكَ، فَإذا بَيَّنَ تَعالى أنَّ ذَلِكَ لا يَحْزُنُهم فَقَدْ صَحَّ أنَّ المُؤْمِنَ آمِنٌ مِن أهْوالِ يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ، وهَذا ضَعِيفٌ؛ لِأنَّ عَذابَ النّارِ عَلى مَراتِبَ فَعَذابُ الكُفّارِ أشَدُّ مِن عَذابِ الفُسّاقِ، وإذا كانَتْ مَراتِبُ التَّعْذِيبِ بِالنّارِ مُتَفاوِتَةً كانَتْ مَراتِبُ الفَزَعِ مِنها مُتَفاوِتَةً، فَلا يَلْزَمُ مِن نَفْيِ الفَزَعِ الأكْبَرِ نَفْيُ الفَزَعِ مِنَ النّارِ.

The third: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the closing of the Fire over its people, so they are struck with a great terror at that. Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar said: the more likely view is that it is the terror of the Fire at the moment of witnessing it, since there is no greater terror than that. So when God Most High declares that this will not grieve them, it is established that the believer is safe from the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. But this is weak, because the punishment of the Fire has degrees: the punishment of the disbelievers is more severe than that of the sinners, and if the degrees of punishment by the Fire vary, the degrees of terror from it also vary. Thus, negating the greatest terror does not necessarily negate terror of the Fire.

الصِّفَةُ الخامِسَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ: هُمُ الحَفَظَةُ الَّذِينَ كَتَبُوا أعْمالَهم وأقْوالَهم، ويَقُولُونَ لَهم مُبَشِّرِينَ: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ .

The fifth description: His saying ﴿and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your day which you were promised"﴾. Al-Dahhak said: they are the guardian angels who recorded their deeds and words, and they say to them, giving good tidings: ﴿This is your day which you were promised.﴾

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾

[The verses mean: "Indeed, those for whom the best reward from Us has preceded, they will be kept far from it (Hell). They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire. The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them, saying: 'This is your day which you were promised.'"]

اعْلَمْ أنَّ مِنَ النّاسِ مَن زَعَمَ أنَّ ابْنَ الزِّبَعْرى لَمّا أوْرَدَ ذَلِكَ السُّؤالَ عَلى الرَّسُولِ ﷺ بَقِيَ ساكِتًا حَتّى أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى هَذِهِ الآيَةَ جَوابًا عَنْ سُؤالِهِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ كالِاسْتِثْناءِ مِن تِلْكَ الآيَةِ، وأمّا نَحْنُ فَقَدَ بَيَّنّا فَسادَ هَذا القَوْلِ، وذَكَرْنا أنَّ سُؤالَهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ وارِدًا، وأنَّهُ لا حاجَةَ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِهِ إلى نُزُولِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ، وإذا ثَبَتَ هَذا لَمْ يَبْقَ هاهُنا إلّا أحَدُ أمْرَيْنِ:

Know that some people claim that when Ibn al-Zib'ara raised that objection to the Messenger (ﷺ), he remained silent until God Most High revealed this verse as an answer to his question, because this verse is like an exception to that verse. As for us, we have already demonstrated the invalidity of this view, and we mentioned that his question was not a valid one, and that there is no need to revelation of this verse to dispel his question. Once this is established, only one of two possibilities remains:

الأوَّلُ: أنْ يُقالَ: إنَّ عادَةَ اللَّهِ تَعالى أنَّهُ مَتى شَرَحَ عِقابَ الكُفّارِ أرْدَفَهُ بِشَرْحِ ثَوابِ الأبْرارِ، فَلِهَذا السَّبَبِ ذَكَرَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ عَقِيبَ تِلْكَ فَهي عامَّةٌ في حَقِّ كُلِّ المُؤْمِنِينَ.

The first: it may be said that it is God Most High's custom that whenever He describes the punishment of the disbelievers, He follows it with a description of the reward of the righteous. For this reason He mentioned this verse right after that one, so it is general in its application to all believers.

الثّانِي: أنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ نَزَلَتْ في تِلْكَ الواقِعَةِ لِتَكُونَ كالتَّأْكِيدِ في دَفْعِ سُؤالِ ابْنِ الزِّبَعْرى، ثُمَّ مَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِعُمُومِ اللَّفْظِ لا بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ، وهو الحَقُّ، أجْراها عَلى عُمُومِها؛ فَتَكُونُ المَلائِكَةُ والمَسِيحُ وعُزَيْرٌ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلامُ داخِلِينَ فِيها، لا أنَّ

The second: this verse was revealed in that incident so as to serve as a confirmation in dismissing Ibn al-Zib'ara's objection. Then, whoever says that the ruling is based on the general wording and not on the specific occasion of revelation (and this is the correct view) applies it in its generality, so that the angels, the Messiah and 'Uzayr (peace be upon them) are included in it, rather than

صفحة ١٩٦
الآيَةَ مُخْتَصَّةٌ بِهِمْ، ومَن قالَ: العِبْرَةُ بِخُصُوصِ السَّبَبِ خَصَّصَ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ بِهَؤُلاءِ فَقَطْ.

the verse being specific to them. And whoever says that the ruling is based on the specific occasion of revelation restricts His saying "Indeed, those who" to these alone.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ فَقالَ صاحِبُ ”الكَشّافِ“: الحُسْنى الخَصْلَةُ المُفَضَّلَةُ، والحُسْنى تَأْنِيثُ الأحْسَنِ، وهي إمّا السَّعادَةُ وإمّا البُشْرى بِالثَّوابِ، وإمّا التَّوْفِيقُ لِلطّاعَةِ، والحاصِلُ أنَّ مُثْبِتِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوا الحُسْنى عَلى وعْدِ العَفْوِ، ومُنْكِرِي العَفْوِ حَمَلُوهُ عَلى وعْدِ الثَّوابِ، ثُمَّ إنَّهُ سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى شَرَحَ مِن أحْوالِ ثَوابِهِمْ أُمُورًا خَمْسَةً:

As for His saying: ﴿has preceded for them from Us the best [reward]﴾, the author of al-Kashshaf said: al-husna is the preferred quality; al-husna is the feminine form of al-ahsan (the best), and it may be happiness, or the good tidings of reward, or divine grace to obey. The point is that those who affirm pardon (al-'afw) interpreted al-husna as the promise of pardon, while those who deny pardon interpreted it as the promise of reward. Then He, glorified and exalted, described five matters concerning their reward:

أحَدُها قَوْلُهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ فَقالَ أهْلُ العَفْوِ: مَعْناهُ أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُخْرَجُونَ، واحْتَجُّوا عَلَيْهِ بِوَجْهَيْنِ:

The first is His saying: ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾. The people of pardon said: its meaning is "they will be removed from it," and they argued for this on two grounds:

الأوَّلُ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ أثْبَتَ الوُرُودَ وهو الدُّخُولُ، فَدَلَّ عَلى أنَّ هَذا الإبْعادَ هو الإخْراجُ.

The first: His saying: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which affirmed the passing over (wurud), which is entering. This shows that this "keeping far" means removal.

الثّانِي: أنَّ إبْعادَ الشَّيْءِ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ لا يَصِحُّ إلّا إذا كانا مُتَقارِبَيْنِ؛ لِأنَّهُما لَوْ كانا مُتَباعِدَيْنِ اسْتَحالَ إبْعادُ أحَدِهِما عَنِ الآخَرِ؛ لَأنَّ تَحْصِيلَ الحاصِلِ مُحالٌ.

The second: keeping one thing far from another is valid only if the two are close to each other; for if they were far apart, it would be impossible to keep one away from the other, because making what is already attained attained again is impossible.

واحْتَجَّ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ عَلى فَسادِ هَذا القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ بِأُمُورٍ:

Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar argued against this first view on several grounds:

أحَدُها: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ يَقْتَضِي أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ في الدُّنْيا ولَيْسَ هَذا حالُ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ لَوْ صَحَّ ذَلِكَ.

The first: His saying ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us﴾ implies that the promise of their reward was given in this world beforehand, and this is not the condition of one who is brought out of the Fire, even if that were valid.

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ تَعالى قالَ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ وكَيْفَ يَدْخُلُ في ذَلِكَ مَن وقَعَ فِيها.

The second: He said ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾, and how can one who has fallen into it be included in this?

وثالِثُها: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ يَمْنَعُ مِن ذَلِكَ.

The third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ and His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ prevent this.

والجَوابُ عَنِ الأوَّلِ: لا نُسَلِّمُ أنْ [ يُقالَ ] المُرادُ مِن قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى﴾ هو أنَّ الوَعْدَ بِثَوابِهِمْ قَدْ تَقَدَّمَ، ولِمَ لا يَجُوزُ أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالعَفْوِ ؟ سَلَّمْنا أنَّ المُرادَ مِنَ الحُسْنى تَقَدُّمُ الوَعْدِ بِالثَّوابِ، لَكِنْ لِمَ قُلْتُمْ: إنَّ الوَعْدَ بِالثَّوابِ لا يَلِيقُ بِحالِ مَن يَخْرُجُ مِنَ النّارِ، فَإنَّ عِنْدَنا المُحابَطَةَ باطِلَةٌ، ويَجُوزُ الجَمْعُ بَيْنَ اسْتِحْقاقِ الثَّوابِ والعِقابِ، وعَنِ الثّانِي: أنّا بَيَّنّا أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ لا يُمْكِنُ إجْراؤُهُ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ إلّا في حَقِّ مَن كانَ في النّارِ، وعَنِ الثّالِثِ: أنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ مَخْصُوصٌ بِما بَعْدَ الخُرُوجِ.

As for the answer to the first: we do not accept that it means the promise of their reward had already been given. Why could it not be that the "best" means the prior promise of pardon? Even if we grant that it means the prior promise of reward, why do you say that a promise of reward is not fitting for the condition of one who comes out of the Fire? For in our view, *muhabata* (the nullification of good deeds by sins) is false, and it is permissible to combine deserving reward and punishment. As for the answer to the second: we have shown that His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ cannot be applied to its apparent meaning except regarding one who was in the Fire. As for the answer to the third: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾ is restricted to what comes after the exit.

أمّا قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ فالفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ هو عَذابُ الكُفّارِ، وهَذا بِطَرِيقِ المَفْهُومِ يَقْتَضِي أنَّهم يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأصْغَرُ، فَإنْ لَمْ يَدُلَّ عَلَيْهِ فَلا أقَلَّ مِن أنْ لا يَدُلَّ عَلى ثُبُوتِهِ ولا عَلى عَدَمِهِ.

As for His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾: the greatest terror is the punishment of the disbelievers. By way of implication (mafhum), this indicates that they may be grieved by the lesser terror; and if it does not indicate this, then at least it does not indicate either its affirmation or its negation.

الوَجْهُ الثّانِي: في تَفْسِيرِ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ أنَّ المُرادَ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهم مِنّا الحُسْنى لا يَدْخُلُونَ النّارَ ولا يَقْرَبُونَها البَتَّةَ، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ بَطَلَ قَوْلُ مَن يَقُولُ: إنَّ جَمِيعَ النّاسِ يَرِدُونَ النّارَ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُونَ إلى الجَنَّةِ؛ لِأنَّ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ مانِعَةٌ مِنهُ، وحِينَئِذٍ يَجِبُ التَّوْفِيقُ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وإنْ مِنكم إلّا وارِدُها﴾ وقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ.

The second view regarding His saying ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾ is that it means those for whom the best has preceded from Us will not enter the Fire and will never draw near to it at all. On this view, the claim of those who say that all people will pass over the Fire and then go out to Paradise is refuted, because this verse prevents it; and then it becomes necessary to reconcile it with His saying ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it﴾, which has already been discussed.

الصِّفَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَها﴾ والحَسِيسُ الصَّوْتُ الَّذِي يُحَسُّ، وفِيهِ سُؤالانِ:

The second description: His saying ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾. The *hasis* is the sound that is perceived. On this there are two questions:

الأوَّلُ: أيُّ وجْهٍ في أنْ لا يَسْمَعُوا حَسِيسَها مِنَ البِشارَةِ، ولَوْ سَمِعُوهُ لَمْ يَتَغَيَّرْ حالُهم ؟

The first: what is the point of their not hearing its sound as a good tiding, since even if they heard it, their condition would not change?

قُلْنا: المُرادُ تَأْكِيدُ بُعْدِهِمْ عَنْها؛ لِأنَّ مَن لَمْ يَدْخُلْها وقَرُبَ مِنها قَدْ يَسْمَعُ حَسِيسَها.

We say: the purpose is to emphasize their distance from it, because one who has not entered it but is near to it may hear its sound.

السُّؤالُ الثّانِي: ألَيْسَ أنَّ أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ يَرَوْنَ أهْلَ النّارِ، فَكَيْفَ لا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَ النّارِ ؟

The second question: do not the people of Paradise see the people of the Fire? So how can they not hear the sound of the Fire?

الجَوابُ: إذا حَمَلْناهُ عَلى التَّأْكِيدِ زالَ هَذا السُّؤالُ.

The answer: if we take it as emphasis, this question disappears.

الصِّفَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وهم في ما اشْتَهَتْ أنْفُسُهم خالِدُونَ﴾ والشَّهْوَةُ طَلَبُ النَّفْسِ لِلَذَّةٍ، يَعْنِي: نَعِيمُها مُؤَبَّدٌ، قالَ العارِفُونَ: لِلنُّفُوسِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْقُلُوبِ شَهْوَةٌ، ولِلْأرْواحِ شَهْوَةٌ، وقالَ الجُنَيْدُ: سَبَقَتِ العِنايَةُ في البِدايَةِ، فَظَهَرَتِ الوِلايَةُ في النِّهايَةِ.

The third description: His saying ﴿and they will abide forever in what their souls desire﴾. *Shahwa* (desire) is the soul's seeking of pleasure; that is, its bliss is everlasting. The gnostics (al-'arifun) said: the souls have a desire, the hearts have a desire, and the spirits have a desire. Al-Junayd said: "Divine care preceded at the beginning, so guardianship (wilaya) appeared at the end."

الصِّفَةُ الرّابِعَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ وفِيهِ وُجُوهٌ:

The fourth description: His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾. On this there are several views:

أحَدُها: أنَّها النَّفْخَةُ الأخِيرَةُ لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿ويَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ في الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾ [النمل: ٨٧] .

The first: it is the final blast, based on His saying: ﴿And the day the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be struck with terror﴾ [al-Naml 27:87].

وثانِيها: أنَّهُ المَوْتُ، قالُوا: إذا اسْتَقَرَّ أهْلُ الجَنَّةِ في الجَنَّةِ وأهْلُ النّارِ في النّارِ، بَعَثَ اللَّهُ تَعالى جِبْرِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ومَعَهُ المَوْتُ في صُورَةِ كَبْشٍ أمْلَحَ فَيَقُولُ: لِأهْلِ الدّارَيْنِ أتَعْرِفُونَ هَذا ؟ فَيَقُولُونَ: لا، فَيَقُولُ: هَذا المَوْتُ، ثُمَّ يَذْبَحُهُ؛ ثُمَّ يُنادِي يا أهْلَ الجَنَّةِ، خُلُودٌ ولا مَوْتَ أبَدًا، وكَذَلِكَ لِأهْلِ النّارِ،

The second: it is death. They said: when the people of Paradise have settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, God Most High sends Gabriel (peace be upon him), and with him Death in the form of a white-speckled ram. He says to the people of both abodes: "Do you recognize this?" They say: "No." He says: "This is Death." Then he slaughters it, and then calls out: "O people of Paradise, eternal abiding with no death ever," and likewise for the people of the Fire.

صفحة ١٩٧
واحْتَجَّ هَذا القائِلُ بِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ﴾ إنَّما ذُكِرَ بَعْدَ قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وهم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾ فَلا بُدَّ وأنْ يَكُونَ لِأحَدِهِما تَعَلُّقٌ بِالآخَرِ، والفَزَعُ الأكْبَرُ الَّذِي هو يُنافِي الخُلُودَ هو المَوْتُ.

This speaker argued that His saying ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ was mentioned after His saying ﴿and they abide therein forever﴾; so one of them must be connected to the other, and the greatest terror which contradicts eternal abiding is death.

وثالِثُها: قالَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ: هو إطْباقُ النّارِ عَلى أهْلِها فَيَفْزَعُونَ لِذَلِكَ فَزْعَةً عَظِيمَةً، قالَ القاضِي عَبْدُ الجَبّارِ: الأوْلى في ذَلِكَ أنَّهُ الفَزَعُ مِنَ النّارِ عِنْدَ مُشاهَدَتِها؛ لِأنَّهُ لا فَزَعَ أكْبَرُ مِن ذَلِكَ، فَإذا بَيَّنَ تَعالى أنَّ ذَلِكَ لا يَحْزُنُهم فَقَدْ صَحَّ أنَّ المُؤْمِنَ آمِنٌ مِن أهْوالِ يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ، وهَذا ضَعِيفٌ؛ لِأنَّ عَذابَ النّارِ عَلى مَراتِبَ فَعَذابُ الكُفّارِ أشَدُّ مِن عَذابِ الفُسّاقِ، وإذا كانَتْ مَراتِبُ التَّعْذِيبِ بِالنّارِ مُتَفاوِتَةً كانَتْ مَراتِبُ الفَزَعِ مِنها مُتَفاوِتَةً، فَلا يَلْزَمُ مِن نَفْيِ الفَزَعِ الأكْبَرِ نَفْيُ الفَزَعِ مِنَ النّارِ.

The third: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the closing of the Fire over its people, so they are struck with a great terror at that. Qadi 'Abd al-Jabbar said: the more likely view is that it is the terror of the Fire at the moment of witnessing it, since there is no greater terror than that. So when God Most High declares that this will not grieve them, it is established that the believer is safe from the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. But this is weak, because the punishment of the Fire has degrees: the punishment of the disbelievers is more severe than that of the sinners, and if the degrees of punishment by the Fire vary, the degrees of terror from it also vary. Thus, negating the greatest terror does not necessarily negate terror of the Fire.

الصِّفَةُ الخامِسَةُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿وتَتَلَقّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ قالَ الضَّحّاكُ: هُمُ الحَفَظَةُ الَّذِينَ كَتَبُوا أعْمالَهم وأقْوالَهم، ويَقُولُونَ لَهم مُبَشِّرِينَ: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ .

The fifth description: His saying ﴿and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your day which you were promised"﴾. Al-Dahhak said: they are the guardian angels who recorded their deeds and words, and they say to them, giving good tidings: ﴿This is your day which you were promised.﴾

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 21, verses 105–111 (part 1 of 2):

Allah's words: ﴿On the day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a written scroll for documents. As We originated the first creation, We shall repeat it; a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing it.﴾ ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Dhikr, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship.﴾ ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾

Know that the implied meaning is: "They will not be grieved by the greatest terror on the day We roll up the heaven," or: "and the angels will receive them on the day We roll up the heaven." It is also read as ﴿On the day the heaven is rolled up﴾ in the passive voice. "Al-sijill" is on the pattern of "al-'itill," and "al-sajl" is on the pattern of "al-dalw," and a vowel with kasra is also reported in it. Regarding "al-sijill" there are two opinions:

The first: It is a name for the scroll (tumar) in which things are written. "Al-kitab" originally is a verbal noun like "al-bina'," and then it is applied to what is written. Whoever reads it as a plural (al-kutub) means "for the written things," i.e., for the many meanings written in it. So the meaning of "rolling up the sijill for the kitab" is that the sijill covers that writing and conceals it, because rolling up is the opposite of unfolding, which reveals. The meaning is: We shall roll up the heaven as the scroll in which things are written is rolled up.

The second opinion: It is not a name for the scroll. Then Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Al-sijill is the name of an angel who rolls up the books of the children of Adam when they are raised to him." This is also related from 'Ali, peace be upon him. Abu al-Jawza' related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it is the name of a scribe who belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is far-fetched, because the scribes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were well known, and none of them was named this. Al-Zajjaj said: "It is the man, in the Abyssinian language." On these views, it is like saying "as Zayd rolls up the book," and the lam in "lil-kitab" is extra, as in His words "radifa lakum." If we say that the intended meaning of al-sijill is the scroll, then the verbal noun, which is rolling (tayy), is in the genitive form with the object, and the agent is omitted; the meaning is "like the rolling of the one who rolls the scroll." This last opinion is that of the majority.

Regarding His words: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾ there are several issues:

The first issue: Al-Farra' said: the speech ends at His words "al-kutub," then He begins: ﴿As We originated﴾. Some said: when He said ﴿And the angels will receive them, saying: "This is your day which you were promised"﴾, He followed it with ﴿On the day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a written scroll for documents﴾, so He described the day with that, then described it with another description, saying: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾.

The second issue: The author of "al-Kashshaf," may Allah have mercy on him, said: ﴿first creation﴾ is the object of "nu'id" (We shall repeat), which is explained by "nu'iduhu." The kaf is restrained by "ma," and the meaning is: We shall repeat the first of creation as We originated it, likening repetition to origination. If you ask, why is "khalq" indefinite? I say: it is like your saying "the first man who came to me was Zayd," meaning "the first of the men," but you made it singular and indefinite to intend their detail, man by man. Likewise, the meaning of "awwal khalq" is "the first of creation" in the sense of "the first of creatures," because "khalq" is a verbal noun that is not pluralized.

The third issue: They differed about the manner of the repetition. Some said: Allah, exalted is He, separates the parts of bodies without annihilating them, then He restores their composition, and that is the repetition. Others said: He, exalted is He, annihilates them completely, then He brings them back into existence in their very same form a second time. This verse is evidence for this view, because He, glory be to Him, likened repetition to origination. Since origination is not an expression for the composition of scattered parts but for existence after non-existence, the situation in repetition must be the same. Those who hold the first view argue with His words: ﴿And the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand﴾ [al-Zumar: 67], which shows that the heavens, while they are rolled up, exist; and with His words: ﴿On the day the earth will be replaced by another earth﴾ [Ibrahim: 48], which shows that the parts of the earth remain but are made into other than the earth.

As for His words: ﴿a promise binding upon Us﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: that "wa'dan" is an emphatic verbal noun, because His words "nu'iduhu" are a promise of repetition.

The second: that the meaning is "a truth binding upon Us," on account of the information about it and the connection of knowledge to its occurrence, since the occurrence of what Allah knows will occur is necessary. Then, exalted is He, confirmed this with His words: ﴿Indeed, We are ever doing it﴾, meaning: We shall certainly do that, and this is an emphasis of the promise He mentioned.

As for His words: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur, after the Dhikr﴾ there are issues:

The first issue: Hamza read "al-Zubur" with a damma on the zay, and the rest read it with a fatha. The word "al-Zabur" is like "al-halub" and "al-rakub." It is said: "zabartu al-kitab," meaning "I wrote the book." "Al-Zubur" with a damma on the zay is the plural of "zibr," like "qishr" and "qushur." The meaning of the two readings is one, because al-Zabur is the book.

The second issue: Regarding al-Zabur and al-Dhikr there are several views:

First: This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Ibn Zayd: al-Zabur is the revealed books, and al-Dhikr is the Book which is the Mother of the Book in heaven, because in it is the writing of everything that will occur, as a lesson for the angels, and the books of the prophets, peace be upon them, are copied from that Book.

Second: al-Zabur is the Qur'an, and al-Dhikr is the Torah. This is the view of Qatadah and al-Sha'bi.

Third: al-Zabur is the Zabur of Dawud, peace be upon him, and al-Dhikr is what is narrated from him, peace be upon him, who said: "Allah existed and there was nothing with Him; then He created the Dhikr."

In my view there is a fourth opinion: that the intended meaning of al-Dhikr is knowledge, i.e., "We wrote that in the Zabur after We had knowledge that is not subject to inattention or forgetfulness." For whoever writes something and commits to it, but inattention is possible for him, is not relied upon; but whoever is not subject to inattention or failure, when he commits to something, that thing is necessarily going to occur.

Page 199

As for His words: ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ there are several views:

First: The earth is the earth of Paradise, and the righteous servants are the believers who act in obedience to Allah, exalted is He. The meaning is that Allah, exalted is He, wrote in the books of the prophets, peace be upon them, and in the Preserved Tablet, that He would make those of His servants who are righteous inherit Paradise. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Suddi and Abu al-'Aliyah. These scholars supported this view with several points:

Firstly: His words: ﴿And He has caused us to inherit the earth; we settle in Paradise wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ [al-Zumar: 74].

Secondly: Because it is the earth which is specific to the righteous, since it was created for them; others who are in Paradise with them are there by way of following. As for the earth of this world, it is for both the righteous and the non-righteous.

Thirdly: Because this earth is mentioned right after the repetition and after the repetition; the earth described in this way can only be Paradise.

Fourthly: It has been reported in a report that it is the earth of Paradise, for it is white and pure.

Second: The intended earth is the earth of this world, for He, glory be to Him, will make the believers inherit it in this world. This is the view of al-Kalbi and Ibn 'Abbas in some narrations. The evidence for this view is His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe﴾ [al-Nur: 55] up to His words: ﴿He will surely make them successors in the earth﴾ [al-Nur: 55], and His words, exalted is He: ﴿Musa said to his people: "Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He causes whom He wills of His servants to inherit it"﴾ [al-A'raf: 128].

Third: It is the Holy Land, which the righteous will inherit. Its evidence is His words: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed﴾ [al-A'raf: 137]. Then, in the end, it will be inherited by the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ) at the descent of 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, His words "this" refer to what is mentioned in this surah of reports, promises, warnings and effective admonitions. "Al-balagh" means sufficiency and that by which the desired aim is reached. It has been said about "al-'abidin" that they are the scholars; it has been said: rather, they are those who act. The better view is that they are those who combine both matters, because knowledge is like a tree and action is like fruit; a tree without fruit is of no benefit, and fruit without a tree does not exist.

* * *

As for His words: ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ there are several issues:

The first issue: He, peace be upon him, was a mercy in religion and in this world. As for religion, he, peace be upon him, was sent when people were in ignorance and error, and the People of the Two Books were in confusion about their religion because of the long passage of time, the breaking of continuous transmission, and the occurrence of disagreement in their books. So Allah, exalted is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) when there was no path for the seeker of truth to attain success and reward. He called them to the truth, showed them the way to reward, legislated rulings for them, and distinguished the lawful from the unlawful. Then, only the one whose aspiration is to seek the truth benefits from this mercy, so he does not rely on blind imitation or on obstinacy and arrogance; and success accompanies him. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing"﴾ [Fussilat: 44] up to His words: ﴿And it is blindness for them﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

As for this world, they were freed through him from much humiliation, fighting and wars, and they were given victory through the blessing of his religion. If it is said: How was he a mercy when he came with the sword and the seizing of wealth? We reply: the answer has several aspects:

First: He came with the sword only against the one who was arrogant and obstinate and did not reflect or contemplate; and among the attributes of Allah are "the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," and then He is an avenger against the disobedient. And He said: ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water﴾ [Qaf: 9], and then it may be a cause of corruption.

Second: Every prophet before our Prophet, when his people denied him, Allah destroyed the deniers by sinking, transformation or drowning; and Allah, exalted is He, delayed the punishment of those who denied our Messenger until death or until the Resurrection. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾ [al-Anfal: 33]. It may be objected: did He not say: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14], and: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73]? We reply: specification of the general does not undermine it.

Third: He, peace be upon him, was at the peak of good character. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great moral character﴾ [al-Qalam: 4]. Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 'Invoke curse upon the polytheists.' He said: 'I was sent only as a mercy, and I was not sent as a punishment.'" And in a narration from Hudhayfah he said: "I am only a human; I become angry as humans become angry. So whichever man I insult or curse, O Allah, make that a blessing for him on the Day of Resurrection."

Fourth: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: ﴿except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ means specifically the believers. The Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Ansari said: the two views return to one meaning, because we have shown that he was a mercy to all if they had reflected upon the signs of Allah and the signs of His Messenger; as for the one who turned away and was arrogant, he fell into trial from his own side, as He said: ﴿And it is blindness for them﴾ [Fussilat: 44].

**Second issue:** The Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites, a theological school that emphasized divine justice and human free will) said: If God willed disbelief from the disbelievers, and did not will from them the acceptance of the Messenger, but willed from them nothing except that they reject him, and created that in them, and created them only in that state, as the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah, the majority Sunni theological position) say, then his sending would necessarily be a vengeance and a punishment upon them, not a mercy. That would contradict this text. It cannot be said that his mission, peace be upon him, is a mercy to the disbelievers in that he did not hasten their punishment in this world, as he hastened the punishment of the other nations. For we say: his being a mercy is of one degree for all, and what you have mentioned for the disbelievers is also obtained by the believers. So it must be that it is a mercy to the disbelievers from the same aspect in which it became a mercy to the believers. Furthermore, the worldly blessings that they mentioned were already obtained by the disbelievers before his mission (ﷺ), just as they were after it. It is also read as ﴿On the day the heaven is rolled up﴾ in the passive voice. Whoever reads it as a plural (al-kutub) means "for the written things," i.e., for the many meanings written in it. So the meaning of "rolling up the sijill for the kitab" is that the sijill covers that writing and conceals it, because rolling up is the opposite of unfolding, which reveals. The meaning is: We shall roll up the heaven as the scroll in which things are written is rolled up.

The second opinion: It is not a name for the scroll. Then Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Al-sijill is the name of an angel who rolls up the books of the children of Adam when they are raised to him." This is also related from 'Ali, peace be upon him. Abu al-Jawza' related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it is the name of a scribe who belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is far-fetched, because the scribes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were well known, and none of them was named this. Al-Zajjaj said: "It is the man, in the Abyssinian language." On these views, it is like saying "as Zayd rolls up the book," and the lam in "lil-kitab" is extra, as in His words "radifa lakum." If we say that the intended meaning of al-sijill is the scroll, then the verbal noun, which is rolling (tayy), is in the genitive form with the object, and the agent is omitted; the meaning is "like the rolling of the one who rolls the scroll." This last opinion is that of the majority.

Regarding His words: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾ there are several issues:

The first issue: Al-Farra' said: the speech ends at His words "al-kutub," then He begins: ﴿As We originated﴾. Some said: when He said ﴿And the angels will receive them, saying: "This is your day which you were promised"﴾, He followed it with ﴿On the day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a written scroll for documents﴾, so He described the day with that, then described it with another description, saying: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We shall repeat it﴾.

The kaf is restrained by "ma," and the meaning is: We shall repeat the first of creation as We originated it, likening repetition to origination. If you ask, why is "khalq" indefinite? I say: it is like your saying "the first man who came to me was Zayd," meaning "the first of the men," but you made it singular and indefinite to intend their detail, man by man. Then, exalted is He, confirmed this with His words: ﴿Indeed, We are ever doing it﴾, meaning: We shall certainly do that, and this is an emphasis of the promise He mentioned.

So the meaning of "rolling up the sijill for the kitab" is that the sijill covers that writing and conceals it, because rolling up is the opposite of unfolding, which reveals. The meaning is: We shall roll up the heaven as the scroll in which things are written is rolled up.

The second opinion: It is not a name for the scroll. Then Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Al-sijill is the name of an angel who rolls up the books of the children of Adam when they are raised to him." This is also related from 'Ali, peace be upon him.
